papers.reason: 为≥65岁ES-SCLC一线免疫联合化疗的真实世界生存获益提供比较基线，影响老年患者治疗选择及 pivotal trial 外推判断。
papers.abstract_en: AIMS: First-line chemoimmunotherapy (ICI-chemo) has become the standard of care for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). However, older adults are underrepresented in pivotal trials due to strict inclusion criteria that limit participation to highly selected, fit patients. Given the limited real-world comparative data, this study aimed to determine whether older adults with ES-SCLC derive greater benefit from ICI-chemo compared with chemotherapy (chemo) alone. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study including ES-SCLC patients aged 65 years or older who started first-line ICI-chemo or chemo between January 2020 and July 2024. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for baseline confounding. The main outcome was overall survival (OS) in the IPTW population. RESULTS: In the IPTW population, median OS was significantly longer in the ICI-chemo group (14.95 months; 95% CI, 12.94-19.91) compared with chemo (10.28 months; 95% CI, 8.11-13.17; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.48-0.91; p = 0.011). Multivariable analysis confirmed that ICI-chemo exposure was independently associated with improved OS (HR, 0.608; 95% CI, 0.440-0.841; p = 0.003). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide comparative evidence of improved survival in association with ICI-chemo compared with chemo in older adults with ES-SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Psilocybin has received increased attention as a potential therapeutic intervention, but it is unclear whether news media reporting reflects the strengths and limitations of the clinical trial evidence. OBJECTIVE: To describe the annual counts of published clinical trials of therapeutic psilocybin and contemporaneous media articles and compare tone, efficacy, and safety messaging. EVIDENCE REVIEW: This systematic review included English-language randomized and nonrandomized trials of psilocybin for clinical indications published from January 1, 2014, to October 10, 2024, and media articles describing its clinical use published from January 1, 2014, to April 22, 2025. Trials were found by searching Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and were characterized by design, indication, use of psychotherapy, and reporting of efficacy and safety. Media articles were found through the Factiva database and were characterized by audience, tone, indication, efficacy claim, and safety content. Data were extracted by 2 reviewers. Risk of bias for randomized clinical trials was assessed descriptively using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. FINDINGS: Annual counts of both published clinical trials (n = 70) and media reports (n = 172) increased from 2018 onward. Depression was the most common clinical indication in trials (47 [67%]) and media articles (138 [80%]), while media articles frequently referenced posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) (74 [43%]) and anxiety (72 [42%]) as clinical indications despite absent and limited trial evidence, respectively, for these conditions. Overall, 49 trials (70%) reported benefit for the primary indication; 125 media articles (73%) made at least 1 positive efficacy claim, and 122 (71%) adopted a favorable tone. Trials typically described small sample sizes of less than 100 participants (65 trials [93%]) and methodologic limitations. Overall, 31 trials (44%) reported safety outcomes, with some (24 [34%]) documenting short-term adverse events, such as transient anxiety, nausea, or headache; long-term safety was rarely assessed (4 trials [6%]). Only 51 media articles (30%) mentioned safety; when harms were discussed, potential long-term psychological risks were sometimes noted (12 articles [7%]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this systematic review of clinical trials and media articles, both reported positive effects of therapeutic psilocybin with similar frequency. Academic publications were more cautious and explicit about methodologic limitations, whereas media reports often presented benefits as established, extrapolated them to indications with little or no trial evidence, and provided less safety information. Clarifying these differences in emphasis may support more transparent public communication of indication-specific evidence and uncertainty as interest in psilocybin-assisted treatments grows.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to preliminarily evaluate the non-inferiority of ERAS-based perioperative management in endoscopic resection for upper gastrointestinal lesions. METHODS: A total of 165 patients with upper gastrointestinal lesions ≤ 2 cm undergoing endoscopic resection (STER, ESD, ESE, or EFTR) were randomized 1:2 to the ERAS group (n = 55) or the conventional recovery after surgery (CRAS) group (n = 110). The primary outcome was postoperative complication rate, with a non-inferiority margin of 5%. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, recovery indicators, length of stay, and hospitalization costs. RESULTS: The risk difference in postoperative complications between the ERAS group and the CRAS group was - 0.91% (90% CI [- 3.97% to 3.83%]), meeting the prespecified criterion for non-inferiority. The ERAS group also showed significantly lower VAS pain scores (0.0 [0.0-3.0] vs. 2.0 [0.0-3.3]; p = 0.020), shorter nasogastric tube duration (3.0 [2.0-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-4.0] days; p < 0.001), and earlier time to first oral water (23.9 [18.5-32.5] vs. 64.7 [56.2-77.0] hours; p < 0.001), first oral feeding (33.2 [22.5-38.5] vs. 70.3 [59.2-79.8] hours; p < 0.001), and first ambulation (36.8 [27.0-45.5] vs. 76.1 [62.0-86.0] hours; p < 0.001). Postoperative length of stay, total length of stay, and hospitalization costs were also significantly reduced (all p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: In this single-center trial involving selected patients with upper gastrointestinal lesions ≤ 2 cm, ERAS met the prespecified criterion for non-inferiority to CRAS with respect to postoperative complications. ERAS was also associated with shorter hospital stays and lower hospitalization costs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Claudin18.2 is a clinically validated target for gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. However, the antigen heterogeneity, low surface density, and issues related to scFv-associated conformational instability and tonic signaling may limit the durability and therapeutic window of Claudin18.2-directed CAR-T cell therapy. Therefore, improving the design of CAR-T cells targeting Claudin18.2 could enhance their effectiveness in treating these cancers. METHODS: We generated third-generation Claudin18.2 CAR-T cells using either a humanized camelid single-domain antibody (VHH) or a conventional scFv as the antigen-recognition module, maintaining an identical CAR backbone for both constructs. To evaluate their performance, we used a gastric cancer cell-line panel with graded Claudin18.2 expression and corresponding xenograft models. We assessed CAR-T cell activity by measuring antigen-dependent cytotoxicity, cytokine secretion (IFN-γ and TNF-α), and reactivity toward antigen-negative targets. In vivo, we examined tumor control, T-cell infiltration, and CD8⁺ T-cell enrichment, and assessed toxicity. Additionally, we investigated the stability of CAR expression, T-cell expansion, and exhaustion-associated phenotypes. Structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the stability of the binding interface of the VHH-Claudin18.2 complex relative to the scFv-Claudin18.2 complex. RESULTS: VHH-based CAR-T cells exhibited superior antigen-dependent activity compared to scFv-based CAR-T cells. VHH-CAR-T cells maintained higher cytotoxicity and IFN-γ and TNF-α secretion even under low antigen density and displayed minimal reactivity against antigen-negative targets. In vivo, VHH-CAR-T cells achieved faster and more durable tumor control, with enhanced intratumoral T-cell infiltration and CD8⁺ T-cell enrichment, without any overt toxicity. Mechanistically, the use of a VHH recognition domain was associated with better preserved surface CAR expression after antigen engagement, expanded more robustly, displayed fewer exhaustion-associated phenotypes, had a higher proportion of central memory T cells, and showed transcriptional enrichment of proliferative and effector programs with restrained exhaustion signatures. Structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations further confirmed that the VHH-Claudin18.2 binding interface was more stable than that of scFv-Claudin18.2. CONCLUSION: Replacing scFv with VHH is associated with enhanced functional performance, persistence, and therapeutic efficacy of Claudin18.2-directed CAR-T. These findings support the further development and translation of VHH-based CAR-T strategies for solid tumor treatment.

papers.authors_conclusion: 现有证据支持对可切除NSCLC采用“新辅助优先”策略；基于主要为跨试验间接比较，单纯新辅助模式疗效与“三明治”模式相当且可能具有成本效益优势，可作为初始策略优先考虑；新辅助术后基于pCR与MRD状态的个体化管理是该领域未来方向。

papers.abstract_en: The application of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has reshaped the perioperative treatment pattern of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Currently, three treatment paradigms have emerged: adjuvant, neoadjuvant alone, and 'sandwich' (neoadjuvant+surgery+adjuvant). Although IMpower010 and KEYNOTE-091 achieved positive results in adjuvant immunotherapy, the negative results of two large phase III studies, BR.31 and ANVIL, raised questions about the generalizability of this model. In contrast, neoadjuvant immunotherapy has shown efficacy in multiple phase III studies. This advantage may stem from the preservation of the intact tumor antigen repertoire and draining lymph node architecture, enabling chemo-immunotherapy to elicit more robust systemic immune responses. Currently, both neoadjuvant alone and 'sandwich' models are recommended by guidelines, but the 5-year overall survival (OS) rates of CheckMate-816 and KEYNOTE-671 are nearly identical (65.4% vs 64.6%), and the pathological complete response (pCR) rate of CheckMate-77T (25.3%) is comparable to that of CheckMate-816 (24%), suggesting that the incremental benefit of extending neoadjuvant cycles and adding postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy in the 'sandwich' model is very limited. In the future, an individualized decision-making model based on pCR and molecular residual disease (MRD) status, such as de-escalation to observation for those achieving pCR with negative MRD, and intensification for those with residual disease or positive MRD, is expected to optimize the balance between treatment intensity and survival benefit. In summary, the existing evidence favors the adoption of a 'neoadjuvant first' strategy for resectable NSCLC. Based mainly on cross-trial indirect comparisons, the neoadjuvant alone model offers comparable efficacy to the 'sandwich' approach with potential cost-effectiveness advantages, and may be preferred as the initial strategy. Individualized post-neoadjuvant management represents the future direction of this field. .

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Vibostolimab, an anti-T-cell immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin and ITIM domains (TIGIT) antibody, showed antitumor activity with pembrolizumab in non-small-cell lung cancer. OBJECTIVE: The KEYVIBE-008 study evaluated vibostolimab coformulated with pembrolizumab (vibostolimab/pembrolizumab) plus etoposide and platinum-based chemotherapy (EP) versus atezolizumab plus EP as first-line therapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. METHODS: Participants aged ≥18 years with untreated extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer were randomized 1:1 to vibostolimab/pembrolizumab (200 mg each) or atezolizumab (1200 mg) every 3 weeks, with EP and cisplatin/carboplatin for the first four cycles. The primary endpoint was overall survival. The prespecified interim analysis included a non-binding futility analysis of overall survival (futility threshold for actual number of events, P = 0.4816). RESULTS: Four hundred and sixty participants were randomized (both arms, n = 230). Median time from randomization to data cutoff (4 June, 2024) was 16.6 (range 11.3‒26.1) months. The prespecified futility criterion for overall survival was met (hazard ratio 1.26; 95% confidence interval 1.00‒1.59; P = 0.9762). There was no difference in progression-free survival (hazard ratio 1.01; 95% confidence interval 0.82‒1.23) or objective response rates (71.7% with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab vs 74.8% with atezolizumab). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 66.8% of participants treated with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab and 57.2% treated with atezolizumab. Immune-mediated adverse events and infusion reactions occurred in 39.3% and 29.7% of participants, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In this interim analysis of vibostolimab/pembrolizumab plus EP versus atezolizumab plus EP as first-line therapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer, the prespecified futility criterion for overall survival was met. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events and immune-mediated adverse events were more frequent with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab versus atezolizumab. Given the overall benefit/risk profile, treatment with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab was discontinued. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov, NCT05224141.

papers.abstract_en: Hypoxia-driven epigenetic remodeling is a critical determinant of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epigenetic mechanisms coordinating hypoxia signaling with tumor microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood. Here, by integrating LUAD cell models, murine tumor models, and spatial transcriptomics with reference-based cell-type deconvolution, we identify SATB2 as a previously unrecognized hypoxia-inducible epigenetic regulator in LUAD. HIF-1α, unlike HIF-2α, directly interacts with the promoter of SATB2, promoting its expression in hypoxic environments. Increased levels of SATB2 have been linked to more severe clinical and pathological characteristics as well as poorer outcomes for patients. Mechanistically, SATB2 physically interacts with HIF-1α and p300, while SATB2 loss reduces H3K27 acetylation and elongating RNA polymerase II occupancy at HIF-1 target loci, supporting a model in which SATB2 facilitates HIF-1α-dependent transcriptional elongation and establishes a positive feedback circuit that amplifies hypoxia-responsive transcriptional programs. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further show that SATB2-associated hypoxic programs are preferentially enriched within malignant tumor niches and are associated with remodeling of the local tumor microenvironment. Functionally, SATB2 promotes LUAD growth, metastasis, angiogenesis, and bevacizumab resistance in a HIF-1α-dependent manner, whereas genetic disruption of SATB2 or pharmacological inhibition of p300 enhances sensitivity to anti-angiogenic therapy. Collectively, these findings identify the SATB2-p300-HIF-1α axis as a hypoxia-responsive epigenetic regulatory mechanism linking transcriptional adaptation to malignant progression and resistance to anti-angiogenic therapy, and provide a preclinical rationale for further investigation of this pathway as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: World Trade Center (WTC)-exposed Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) rescue/recovery workers have an elevated risk of smoking-related morbidity. Despite access to free tobacco cessation treatment, some individuals in this population continue to smoke. In other settings, opt-out treatment approaches increase treatment initiation, but effectiveness in occupational health programs is unclear. Accordingly, we (1) assessed whether an opt-out strategy increases engagement with a Tobacco Cessation Program and (2) identified factors associated with engagement. METHODS: This was a randomized trial among FDNY firefighters and Emergency Medical Service (EMS) who self-reported smoking and were eligible for the WTC Health Program Lung Cancer Screening Program. 1:1 randomization occurred prior to contact for opt-out recruitment with Enhanced Care treatment (Opt-Out/Enhanced) or opt-in recruitment with Standard Care treatment (Opt-In/Standard). Opt-Out/Enhanced included proactive outreach and tailored biofeedback during counseling; Opt-In/Standard included participant-initiated engagement and standard counseling. Both groups were offered identical no-cost pharmacotherapy (varenicline). Engagement was defined as: consented enrollment (expressed interest and provided informed consent) and treatment initiation (attendance at ≥1 counseling session). Engagement differences were evaluated using logistic regression; sociodemographic and health-related factors were characterized descriptively without formal testing due to small numbers. RESULTS: Overall, 312 individuals were randomized (Opt-Out/Enhanced, n = 156 and Opt-In/Standard, n = 156). Engagement was low (7.4%). Consented enrollment (n = 23; OR = 3.05; 95% CI = 1.11-9.72) and treatment initiation (n = 18; OR = 2.08; 95% CI = 0.72-6.73) were higher in Opt-Out/Enhanced versus Opt-In/Standard. Treatment initiators had a median age of 60.5 (vs 65.0 years among non-initiators); 38.9% were EMS (vs 18.0%), 22.2% were female (vs 6.9%), 77.8% had a prior cessation attempt (vs 23.5%), and 55.6% had abnormal lung function (vs 32.9%). Participants were too few to analyze cessation outcomes in depth. CONCLUSIONS: Despite low engagement overall, opt-out treatment had higher engagement with tobacco cessation treatment. This supports other work that has found opt-out treatment to be encouraged for hard-to-reach populations.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Lung resection is the standard curative treatment for resectable lung cancer; however, postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) and prolonged hospital length of stay (LOS) remain major barriers to recovery and healthcare efficiency. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) and prehabilitation are distinct perioperative strategies that differ in their timing, intervention components, and mechanisms of action, but both aim to optimize patients' perioperative condition and improve postoperative recovery. However, their effectiveness compared with conventional perioperative care based solely on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) has not been comprehensively synthesized. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of ERAS and prehabilitation in reducing PPCs, shortening LOS, and improving patient-reported outcomes following pulmonary resection for lung cancer. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs involving adults undergoing pulmonary resection for primary lung cancer. Searches of PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, CINAHL Complete, RISS, KISS, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform identified studies published between January 2015 and May 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled odds ratios (ORs) for PPCs and mean differences (MDs) for LOS. Patient-reported outcomes were synthesized narratively according to the SWiM guideline. RESULTS: Ten RCTs involving 1,569 participants met the inclusion criteria. ERAS and prehabilitation significantly reduced PPCs compared with conventional perioperative care (OR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.36-0.65, p < 0.001). The exploratory pooled analysis suggested a shorter postoperative LOS (MD = -2.30 days, 95% CI = -3.58 to -1.01); however, heterogeneity was considerable (I 2 = 97.9%), and the 95% prediction interval crossed the null. Narrative synthesis demonstrated consistent improvements in anxiety, depression, postoperative pain, pulmonary function, quality of life, and functional recovery. CONCLUSION: ERAS and prehabilitation are effective perioperative strategies for improving outcomes after pulmonary resection for lung cancer. Their implementation in routine clinical practice may reduce postoperative complications, accelerate recovery, and improve healthcare efficiency. Further multicenter RCTs are needed to optimize intervention components, standardize outcome measures, and strengthen evidence for long-term and patient-reported outcomes. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: CRD420261373242.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dexmedetomidine has increasingly been incorporated into opioid-sparing anesthetic strategies during video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) because of its analgesic properties and minimal respiratory depression. However, dexmedetomidine remains associated with dose-related hemodynamic adverse effects, particularly bradycardia and hypotension. We evaluated whether a reduced-dose dexmedetomidine regimen decreases intraoperative opioid requirements while maintaining acceptable hemodynamic safety during VATS. METHODS: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 68 patients undergoing VATS were randomly assigned to either a dexmedetomidine group or a control group (34 patients each). The dexmedetomidine group received a loading dose of 0.5 µg/kg followed by continuous infusion at 0.5 µg/kg/h during surgery. The control group received conventional fentanyl-based anesthesia. The primary outcome was maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), postoperative respiratory complications, and perioperative safety outcomes. RESULTS: Maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (18.7 vs. 33.2 µg, P = 0.009). Postoperative pain scores, rescue analgesic requirements, PONV, and respiratory complications were comparable between groups. However, the dexmedetomidine group demonstrated a higher incidence of intraoperative bradycardia (23.5% vs. 0%, P = 0.005) and postoperative hypotension during PACU stay (23.5% vs. 2.9%, P = 0.027). These hemodynamic events were transient and responsive to pharmacologic intervention. CONCLUSIONS: Dexmedetomidine-based opioid-sparing anesthesia reduced maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl administration during VATS. However, the reduction was modest, was not associated with clear postoperative benefits, and was accompanied by increased bradycardia and hypotension. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05431322), registered on 14 June 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05431322 .

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis have the worst prognosis. Despite their involvement in initial assessment, the relationship between Primary Care Physician availability and metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis remains unexplored. Our objective was to determine whether Primary Care Physician availability is associated with patients having metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis. METHODOLOGY: This was a cross-sectional study of patients aged ≥ 18 and diagnosed with breast, colorectal, liver, lung, ovarian, pancreatic, or prostate cancer from 2015 to 2019. Population-based Texas and California cancer registries were used for patient data. The main exposure was county-level Primary Care Physician density per 3500 individuals. Additional exposures included demographic factors, insurance, rural-urban continuum codes, county poverty rates, and US State at Diagnosis. The primary outcome was adjusted odds of metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis. Subgroup analyses based on insurance type, age group, and metropolitan residence were performed. Models were stratified by cancer type. RESULTS: Overall, 708,451 patients were included. On combined multivariable analysis, with each additional Primary Care Physician per 3500 individuals, the odds for primary outcome decreased by 2% to 6%. In a stratified analysis using Primary Care Physician density per 3500 individuals as a categorical variable, compared with counties with < 1 Primary Care Physician, counties with 3 or more Primary Care Physicians had reduced odds of primary outcome for multiple cancer types with no statistically significant difference for counties with 1-1.9 Primary Care Physicians. CONCLUSION: Increased Primary Care Physician availability was associated with a nonlinear decrease in odds for metastatic cancer at diagnosis. Thus, increasing physician density can possibly lower the likelihood of metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: Single-fraction stereotactic body radiotherapy (SF-SBRT) represents one of the most advanced frontiers in modern radiation oncology. While ultra-hypofractionation has entered everyday clinical practice in different fields of the oncological care, curative treatments in one session are increasingly attractive for the potential favorable combination of logistic advantages with safety and clinical outcomes. This collaborative systematic review promoted by the ESTRO SBRT Focus Group in participation with members of different disease-site Focus Groups collects the available data in support of SF-SBRT for the curative treatment of the main extracranial primary tumors. The findings highlight that, for specific anatomical sites, SF-SBRT is both safe and effective though the results emphasize the critical importance of careful patient selection and mandatory technological requirements for treatment planning and delivery. This collaborative work provides a comprehensive overview of current evidence and identifies key knowledge gaps for future investigation and upcoming clinical trials.

papers.abstract_en: Dysregulated splicing factors play critical roles in tumor progression. Here, we identify family with sequence similarity 50 member A (FAM50A) as a pivotal oncogenic splicing factor involved in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Multi-omics and multi-cohort analyses revealed that FAM50A is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with a poor prognosis. Functional studies demonstrated that FAM50A promotes ESCC proliferation and migration both in vitro and in vivo, primarily through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs) and focal adhesion kinase (FAK). We further characterized the FAM50A-binding RNA motif and established its transcriptome-wide splicing landscape. Notably, we identified a novel FAM50A-dependent backsplicing event that generates circSDK1, which originates from exons 2-4 of the sidekick cell adhesion molecule 1 (SDK1) pre-mRNA. Mechanistically, circSDK1 binds to dual-specificity phosphatase 22 (DUSP22) and occupies its phosphatase domain, inhibiting the DUSP22-mediated dephosphorylation of MAPKs and FAK and thereby sustaining their activation. Furthermore, the transcription factor TFAP2C increased FAM50A expression. Finally, we identified rifabutin as a small-molecule inhibitor of FAM50A and confirmed its anti-tumor efficacy in cell-derived xenograft, patient-derived organoid, and patient-derived xenograft models. In summary, FAM50A promotes ESCC progression via the FAM50A/circSDK1/DUSP22 axis, leading to MAPKs and FAK activation. Genetic or pharmacological targeting of FAM50A with rifabutin represents a promising therapeutic strategy for ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchiectasis in women of reproductive age is increasingly recognized, yet data on fertility and pregnancy outcomes remain limited. RESEARCH QUESTION: What are fertility characteristics, pregnancy outcomes, and patient-reported reproductive health experiences in women with bronchiectasis? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study across EMBARC-affiliated centers including women with bronchiectasis and pregnancy between 2012 and 2023. Clinical, pulmonary, obstetric, and neonatal data were collected. In parallel, an international patient survey assessed fertility, pregnancy, and hormonal influences on disease. Statistical analyses included comparative and correlation testing. RESULTS: Eighty-three women contributed data from 121 pregnancies and 123 neonates. Mean age at conception was 29.5 years. Assisted reproductive technologies were used in 32.1% of pregnancies, more frequently in primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) than other etiologies (48.5% vs. 8.7%, P=0.004). Lung function remained stable during and after pregnancy. Exacerbations occurred in 58.6% of pregnancies. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks and mean birth weight was 2.99 kg. Pre-pregnancy FEV1 correlated with birth weight (ρ=0.42, P=0.001) and gestational age (ρ=0.25, P=0.042). Neonatal outcomes were generally favorable. Survey data (n=629) demonstrated an early onset of menopause in women with bronchiectasis diagnosed before age 50 years compared to after 50 years. Women with PCD reported difficulties conceiving more often than women with early onset bronchiectasis without PCD. INTERPRETATION: Pregnancy in women with bronchiectasis is frequently complicated by exacerbations and low neonatal birth weight. Subfertility is primarily driven by PCD, while non-PCD bronchiectasis shows rates similar to the general population. Pre-pregnancy lung function is associated with neonatal outcomes, supporting the importance of pulmonary optimization and multidisciplinary care before and during pregnancy.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Opioid misuse is a major public health concern, and unused prescription opioids can contribute to this problem. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the proportion of unused opioids among patients discharged from the emergency department (ED) for acute pain, evaluate opioid storage and disposal practices, and identify factors that may motivate patients to return unused opioids. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study, which was a preplanned substudy of a Canadian multicenter prospective cohort study (Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group [OPUM] study, with recruitment beginning in May 2019 and follow-up ending in January 2024), included consecutive patients aged 18 years or older discharged from the EDs of 7 hospitals in Québec and Ontario with an opioid prescription for an acute pain condition. Participants were followed up at 2 weeks and 3 months. EXPOSURE: Opioid prescription for acute pain at ED discharge. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were the proportion of participants with unused opioids at 2 weeks and 3 months after ED discharge, opioid storage practices at 2 weeks, and opioid disposal practices at 3 months. RESULTS: Of 2590 enrolled participants in the cohort, 2047 (79.0%) completed the 2-week follow-up and 1835 (70.8%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Among participants who completed the 3-month follow-up, mean (SD) age was 51.3 (15.4) years, 947 (51.6%) were male, and mean pain intensity score at triage was 7.1 (2.3) out of 10. At 2 weeks, 1521 of 1811 participants (84.0%; 95% CI, 82.2%-85.6%) reported unused opioids; 102 of 1525 (6.7%; 95% CI, 5.5%-8.1%) stored their opioids in a locked area and 393 of 1525 (25.8%; 95% CI, 23.6%-28.0%) out of reach of children or teenagers. At 3 months, 926 of 1495 (61.9%; 95% CI, 59.4%-64.4%) reported unused opioids, kept mostly for possible future pain (534 [57.7%; 95% CI, 54.4%-60.9%]) or because participants forgot or lacked time to return them (262 [28.3%; 95% CI, 25.4%-31.3%]). Only 614 of 1835 participants (33.5%; 95% CI, 31.3%-35.7%) indicated they would voluntarily return opioids to the pharmacy if prompted, while 479 (26.1%; 95% CI, 24.1%-28.2%) would not return them regardless of incentive offered. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, 3 months after their ED visit, many participants kept unused prescription opioids at home under suboptimal storage conditions; only one-third were willing to return their opioids to a pharmacy, while more than one-fourth were not. These findings support tailoring opioid prescriptions to individual patient needs to reduce unused medication, alongside strengthening take-back networks and enhancing patient education on safe use, storage, and disposal of opioids.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The role of real-world data in oncology has been substantially increasing, helping to answer clinically unmet needs. No valid framework for real-world data is currently available for the evaluation of surrogate endpoints, with no intermediate clinical endpoint (ICE) being validated as a surrogate for overall survival (OS) across most cancer types. METHODS: A real-world retrospective cohort study was conducted using the nationwide US Flatiron Health database. Four ICEs were evaluated real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), and three exposure-derived endpoints: Time to Next line of Therapy (TTNT), Time to Last Treatment Administration (TTLA) of first line therapy, and Time to End of First-Line Therapy (TTEFL). Two conditions were evaluated to establish surrogacy: correlation between ICE and OS (condition 1), and correlation of group effects (condition 2). RESULTS: A total of 19,164 patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC) were included. Median OS was 36.3 (95%CI, 35.6-37.2) months across the study population. For condition 1, a high correlation was found between each of rwPFS, TTNT and TTLA, and OS (Kendall's tau [τ] ≥ 0.5; R2 ≥ 0.7 between 36-month OS and 12-month rates for each ICE across subgroups of interest). For condition 2, group effects were found to be strongly correlated only between rwPFS and OS (R2 ≥ 0.7 across each subgroup comparison). CONCLUSION: Among patients with MBC, rwPFS is a strong surrogate for OS. This study establishes a novel framework applicable to real-world data for the validation of intermediate clinical endpoints. This study can serve as a blueprint for future efforts of real-world data analysis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung transplantation is a feasible therapeutic option for irreversible lung injury caused by COVID-19, but comprehensive mid-term outcome data remain limited. This study evaluated outcomes after lung transplantation for COVID-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome (CARDS) and post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (CPF) using a national registry. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing database from 2020 through 2024. Recipient characteristics, perioperative complications, and graft failure-free survival were analyzed in adult lung transplant recipients with a primary diagnosis of CARDS, CPF, or non-COVID restrictive lung disease (NCRLD). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and multivariate logistic regression were performed to adjust for potential confounders. RESULTS: During the study period, 256 transplants were performed for CARDS, 338 for CPF, and 8071 for NCRLD. Post-COVID-19 recipients were younger (54 vs. 64 years, p<0.001) and required a higher level of care preoperatively than NCRLD recipients. Posttransplant, post-COVID-19 recipients experienced higher rates of posttransplant ECMO (22.6% vs. 10.3%, p<0.001), ventilation >48 hours (67.5% vs. 43.3%, p<0.001), new dialysis (11.0% vs. 7.9%, p=0.012), and acute rejection (7.7% vs. 5.5%, p=0.026). Graft failure-free survival was equivalent throughout the first year posttransplant between the post-COVID-19 and NCRLD recipients and, after IPTW for age and other confounders, was equivalent for up to 3 years (Hochberg-adjusted p=0.118). CONCLUSIONS: Lung transplantation for post-COVID-19 lung damage yields comparable short-term and mid-term survival outcomes despite higher perioperative morbidity and resource utilization. Long-term studies are needed to assess chronic lung allograft dysfunction in this population.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during non-thermal, non-tumescent (NTNT) ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, Revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes (PROs) based on a HASTI (Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, Itching) symptom questionnaire and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 week, 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months post procedure. Baseline and 12 months post procedure were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted p = 0.03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The InVera Infusion device provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Whether lifetime lung function trajectories and spirometry patterns are associated with Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA) is unknown. We aimed to investigate this association to widen the understanding of OSA pathophysiology. METHODS: We previously identified six FEV1/FVC (forced expiratory volume in the first second/forced vital capacity) and five FVC trajectories within a population-based prospective cohort (n = 2422) using spirometry assessed at ages 7, 13, 18, 43, 50, and 53 years. These trajectories were combined into four lifetime spirometry patterns: restrictive-only, obstructive-only, mixed, and reference (normal), which were our exposure variables. Outcomes were medically-confirmed OSA in midlife and probable-OSA defined using the STOP-Bang questionnaire. Associations were assessed using logistic regression models. RESULTS: The 'restrictive-only' spirometry pattern was associated with medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 2.5; 95% CI 1.5, 4.3). In addition, restriction-confirmatory low total lung capacity and reduced functional residual capacity were associated with increased odds of medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 1.4; 0.9, 2.1 and OR = 1.7; 1.1, 2.6, respectively, per one SD reduction in volume). The results were similar for probable OSA. These associations held when controlled for BMI and central obesity and were independent of childhood lung function. Neither transfer factor for carbon monoxide (TLco) nor transfer coefficient (Kco) was associated with OSA. CONCLUSION: We provide first evidence that lifetime lung restriction is related to middle-age OSA. While this information may be used to incidentally flag middle-age OSA risk and vice versa, further research is encouraged to confirm the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The benefit of routine prophylactic antibiotics for clean laparoscopic adnexal surgery remains unclear. We evaluated whether pre-incision cefazolin reduces the incidence of 30-day surgical site infections (SSIs), and we identified perioperative risk factors for SSIs. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using clinical data from Osaka University and six affiliated hospitals. Among 1,865 patients who underwent laparoscopic adnexal surgery for benign conditions, 1,678 were included after specified exclusions. Patients received either pre-incision cefazolin (n = 1,415) or no prophylaxis (n = 263) according to institutional policy. The primary outcome was the incidence of SSI during the 30-day postoperative interval, classified according to CDC criteria. The association between prophylaxis and SSI was evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Propensity scores were estimated using age, body mass index, diabetes mellitus, endometriosis, and previous abdominal surgery. Risk factors for SSI were assessed using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed by repeating the same IPTW procedure within specified subgroups, and procedure-specific supplementary analyses were performed for ovarian cystectomy. RESULTS: SSI occurred in 1.1% of patients in both groups: 16/1,415 in the cefazolin group and 3/263 in the non-antibiotic group. In IPTW-adjusted analyses, the incidence of SSI did not differ between groups (1.1% vs. 1.2%; p = 0.915). In multivariable analysis, operative time ≥120 min was associated with SSI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.41-8.85). In supplementary analyses restricted to an ovarian cystectomy subgroup, uterine manipulator use was associated with SSI (aOR 4.03, 95% CI 1.26-12.90). CONCLUSION: Routine prophylactic cefazolin was not associated with a significantly lower incidence of 30-day SSI after clean laparoscopic adnexal surgery. Given few SSI events and the potential for residual confounding, our findings support further evaluation of a selective rather than routine approach to prophylactic antibiotic use.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal cancer (EC) is a highly prevalent and aggressive gastrointestinal malignancy. Late diagnosis and heterogeneous responses to chemoradiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapies severely challenge clinical management. Accumulating evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis influences esophageal mucosal malignant transformation, tumor progression, and therapeutic outcomes through the gut-esophageal axis. However, most existing research remains correlational. To bridge this gap, this review critically synthesizes the dysbiosis signatures of EC and establishes a five-tier evidence grading framework to rigorously distinguish causal mechanisms from preclinical inferences. This microbial regulation is predominantly driven by metabolite-mediated signaling, remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment (TME), intestinal barrier disruption, and oncogenic pathway activation. We functionally classify EC-associated dysbiosis into pro-tumorigenic, anti-tumorigenic, and context-dependent taxa, emphasizing a multidimensional ecosystem perspective. Furthermore, we evaluate the utility of gut microbial signatures as predictive biomarkers for neoadjuvant therapy and prognosis. Microbiota-targeted intervention strategies, including fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), microecological preparations, and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), have entered clinical exploration as adjunctive approaches to optimize treatment efficacy. Finally, we address current translational barriers and propose future directions, emphasizing multi-omics integration, spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI). This provides an objective, mechanistically grounded framework for advancing microbiota-guided personalized oncology in EC.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: The question of whether inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) increase the risk of open-angle glaucoma (OAG) has produced conflicting data on short-term effects, but no study has evaluated their long-term effects. We assessed whether long-term cumulative ICS use is associated with an increased risk of incident OAG among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). PATIENTS AND METHODS: The United Kingdom Clinical Practice Research Datalink was used to form a cohort of patients with COPD, aged 40 years or more, who initiated an inhaled maintenance treatment, between September 2013 and March 2021. Subjects were followed until the occurrence of the first OAG diagnosis. Using a nested case-control design, each OAG case was matched with up to 100 concurrently glaucoma-free controls using risk-set sampling. Conditional logistic regression was used to compute the adjusted odds ratio of incident OAG associated with cumulative ICS exposure, as an estimate of the hazard ratio (HR) and its 95% confidence interval (CI). RESULTS: The COPD cohort included 84,564 subjects, with 732 developing OAG (incidence rate 2.64 per 1000 person-years) and 56% having used an ICS since cohort entry. The adjusted HR of OAG associated with any ICS use since cohort entry, compared with non-use, was 1.14 (95% CI, 0.94-1.38). The HR was 1.11 (95% CI, 0.83-1.48) for total cumulative dose ≥365 mg and 1.23 (95% CI, 0.90-1.68) for over 3 years since ICS initiation. CONCLUSION: This large cohort study did not observe a statistically significant increase in the risk of OAG with ICS use, including long-term use and higher cumulative doses, among patients with COPD.

papers.abstract_en: The number of very elderly patients presenting with end-stage knee osteoarthritis (OA) is rising rapidly, yet the comparative merits of medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in this group remain insufficiently characterised. We compared the perioperative safety and short-term clinical and patient-reported efficacy of the two procedures in patients aged 75 years and older with isolated medial-compartment OA. This single-centre retrospective cohort study compared patients aged ≥ 75 years undergoing primary medial UKA or TKA for isolated medial-compartment OA between January 2018 and December 2022. Among 268 eligible patients (68 UKA and 200 TKA), 1:2 nearest-neighbour propensity-score matching, incorporating operating surgeon together with demographic, comorbidity, radiographic and baseline functional covariates, yielded 60 UKA and 120 TKA patients. Perioperative outcomes, KSS, OKS, pain VAS, ROM, postoperative FJS-12, complications, readmission, reoperation and satisfaction were compared over 24-36 months. Standardised mean differences assessed baseline balance; treatment-effect estimates, risk differences and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Matching yielded 180 patients, with all post-match absolute SMDs < 0.10 (maximum 0.087). UKA was associated with shorter operative time (64.3 vs. 84.2 min), lower estimated blood loss (99.9 vs. 183.6 mL), smaller haemoglobin decline (1.5 vs. 2.6 g/dL), shorter stay (3.0 vs. 5.2 days) and earlier independent walking (18.3 vs. 29.6 h). Final KSS components were similar; UKA showed higher OKS and FJS-12, greater knee flexion and lower pain VAS. Complications occurred in 3/60 UKA (5.0%) and 19/120 TKA (15.8%; risk difference - 10.8% points, 95% CI - 19.4 to - 2.3; sensitivity-analysis adjusted OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.09-0.92). Transfusion was infrequent (1.7% vs. 3.3%); readmission and reoperation showed no clear difference. Final satisfaction was 98.3% versus 86.7% (risk difference + 11.7% points, 95% CI 4.8-18.6). In carefully selected patients aged ≥ 75 years with isolated medial-compartment OA, medial UKA was associated with lower measured perioperative burden and more favourable patient-reported outcomes than TKA over 24-36 months. The observed difference in complications should be interpreted cautiously because event counts were small and findings were sensitive to the choice of statistical test. Retrospective allocation, surgeon and implant heterogeneity, potential residual confounding and limited follow-up preclude causal or long-term durability conclusions.

papers.abstract_en: Introduction Respiratory muscle impairment is common in patients with severe emphysema, primarily driven by lung hyperinflation. Endobronchial valve (EBV) treatment reduces hyperinflation and may restore respiratory mechanics in this patient population. Our aim was to investigate changes in neural drive and respiratory muscle recruitment following EBV treatment. Methods EBV-eligible emphysema patients from our prior study on diaphragm function were prospectively enrolled (NCT04735731). Respiratory muscle activation and timing were assessed using surface electromyography at baseline and 6 weeks following EBV treatment. Additionally, an age-matched control group without respiratory symptoms was included for comparison. Results We included 25 patients who underwent EBV treatment (mean FEV1 28% predicted, mean RV 233% predicted) and 12 controls. The inspiratory time (Ti) to total time of respiratory cycle (Ttot) ratio (0.35 vs 0.53; p=0.003) was significantly lower in patients compared to controls. Activity of the diaphragm (4.7 vs 0.9 µV; p<0.001) and intercostal muscles (1.2 vs 0.4 µV; p<0.001) during tidal breathing was significantly higher in patients. Furthermore, tonic (end-expiratory) activity of the diaphragm (1.4 vs 0.6 µV; p=0.012) and intercostal muscles (1.4 vs 0.6 µV; p=0.003) was significantly higher as well. Following EBV treatment, all measured outcomes improved significantly, approaching the values observed in the control group. Conclusion These findings indicate that neural drive and respiratory muscle effort are significantly elevated in severe emphysema patients. By reducing lung hyperinflation, endobronchial valve treatment reduces this load, resulting in improved respiratory mechanics and decreased work of breathing, an important contributor to dyspnoea severity.

papers.abstract_en: Bone metastasis of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) directly leads to poor prognosis. This study aimed to dissect the stromal landscape of LUAD with bone metastases. Unsupervised clustering of scRNA-seq data from LUAD patients with bone metastasis identifies stromal subsets. Pseudotime analysis combined with CytoTRACE stemness scoring reconstructs mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) differentiation trajectories, while CellChat characterizes cell-cell communication networks among MSC subpopulations. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) specific to functionally distinct MSC subsets are subjected to LASSO-Cox regression for construction of a prognostic RiskScore model, which is validated in independent bulk RNA-seq cohorts regarding overall survival, immune cell infiltration, and drug sensitivity. A distinct high-stemness MSC C1 subpopulation is localized at the bifurcation point of two divergent differentiation trajectories toward a matrix-remodeling fate and a secretory, immunomodulatory phenotype. The RiskScore model stratifies patients into low- and high-risk groups with divergent overall-survival outcomes. Reduced infiltration of cytotoxic lymphocytes is observed in high-risk patients, and higher drug sensitivity within the high-risk subgroup. In vitro assays verify that LDHA knockdown impairs proliferation and migration in A549 cells. This study provides a rationale for targeting stroma-derived genes in risk-adapted therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the malignant tumor with the highest incidence and mortality rates worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for approximately 85% of cases. Radical surgical resection serves as the primary curative modality for patients with resectable NSCLC; however, postoperative recurrence persists in a subset of patients, thereby compromising long-term survival outcomes. Consequently, the precise prediction of postoperative recurrence risk, identification of high-risk populations, and formulation of individualized adjuvant therapy and surveillance strategies are of paramount importance for improving patient prognosis. In recent years, fueled by the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and liquid biopsy technologies, the prediction of postoperative recurrence in NSCLC has progressively transitioned toward greater precision and personalization. This review summarizes the current applications of traditional predictive models, AI-based models, and liquid biopsy techniques in forecasting NSCLC recurrence following surgery, evaluating their respective strengths and limitations. Furthermore, it provides insights into future research trajectories. .

papers.abstract_en: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit remarkable functional heterogeneity, with conserved subtypes observed across diverse malignancies. However, their shared roles in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) and their dynamic plasticity remain incompletely understood. In this study, through integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling across four cancer types, we identified two distinct immunomodulatory CAF states, termed antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) and matrix-producing CAFs (mCAFs). Across multiple solid tumors, apCAFs were associated with enhanced anti-tumor immune features and favorable prognosis, whereas mCAFs were associated with immunosuppressive characteristics and poorer clinical outcomes. Spatial analyses revealed distinct localization patterns of apCAFs and mCAFs within the TME. Functionally, patient-derived apCAFs promoted T-cell migration, proliferation, and activation, whereas mCAFs suppressed these responses in vitro. Pan-cancer analyses further revealed a strong inverse correlation between apCAF and mCAF abundance across tumor tissues. Mechanistically, IFN-γ and TGF-β-associated signaling contexts were linked to distinct CAF transcriptional programs, with IFN-γ promoting apCAF-associated features and TGF-β favoring mCAF-associated features, suggesting a potential role of cytokine context in shaping CAF state heterogeneity. Clinically, apCAFs correlated with favorable immunotherapy response, whereas mCAFs predicted poor therapeutic outcomes. Collectively, these findings identify conserved immunomodulatory CAF subtypes across cancers, reveal distinct cytokine-associated CAF programs, and support stromal reprogramming as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Despite strong evidence supporting perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) for patients undergoing lung cancer surgery, little is known about factors that may influence implementation prior to program rollout, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Guided by the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0), this study aimed to identify anticipated barriers and facilitators to inform program refinement and future implementation strategies. METHODS: A descriptive qualitative design was used. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nurses from the thoracic surgery department of a tertiary hospital in China (September-November 2025). Guided by the four CFIR 2.0 domains (innovation, outer setting, inner setting, individuals), directed content analysis was performed based on nurses' perspectives. RESULTS: Sixteen nurses were interviewed, representing diverse roles: Ward/ICU frontline staff nurses, charge nurses, unit secretaries, administrative nurses and nurse managers. Relevant constructs included 22 of the 29 CFIR 2.0 constructs and 8 subconstructs. Facilitators spanned: innovation (source, evidence base, relative advantage, trialability); outer setting (financing, policy, external pressure); inner setting (relational connections, communication, culture, incentive systems); and individual factors (team needs, leadership/practitioner capability, motivation). Barriers comprised: innovation (adaptability, complexity, cost); outer setting (local condition, partnerships and connections); inner setting (structural characteristics, compatibility, access to knowledge and information); and individuals (recipient needs, capability). Notably, implementation concerns differed across nursing roles, reflecting role heterogeneity and underscoring the need for tailored implementation strategies. CONCLUSION: Implementation of perioperative PR for patients undergoing lung cancer surgery is influenced by multilevel factors spanning innovation, outer setting, inner setting, and individuals determinants. Differences in concerns across nursing roles highlight the importance of role-tailored implementation strategies. These findings provide a foundation for optimizing implementation approaches and may facilitate the sustainable integration of evidence-based PR into routine practice, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare settings.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Porcine xenotransplantation offers a promising solution to human organ shortages, yet cross-species transmission of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) remains a major safety barrier. Current risk assessments predominantly rely on a single reference genome, creating a distinct blind spot regarding ERV diversity and structural variation across diverse genetic backgrounds. We profiled ERV loci across five chromosome-level pig genome assemblies (Bama miniature pig, Duroc, Meishan, Ningxiang, and USMARC), characterizing structural completeness, phylogenetic relationships, relative insertion ages, and host-gene/QTL genomic context. ERVs were identified with the LTRharvest/LTRdigest pipeline, annotated by Pfam domain screening, and classified as complete, near-complete, or partial. Phylogenetic analysis used maximum-likelihood inference, insertion age was estimated from paired long terminal repeat (LTR) divergence, and ERV-proximal genes within 10 kb were analyzed for Gene Ontology (GO)/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment and tissue expression. RESULTS: Across the five chromosome-level assemblies, the paired-LTR-anchored catalog comprised 23,767 ERV candidates in the main autosome/chrX analysis set, including 75 structurally complete, 322 near-complete, and 23,370 partial loci. An additional 86 chrY records were detected in assemblies with chrY and were all classified as partial. Complete-ERV insertion-age profiles showed assembly-level variation, although Kruskal-Wallis tests did not detect a significant overall difference among assemblies. The five-assembly shared ERV-proximal host-gene set contained 278 genes at the 10 kb window; this set decreased to 229 genes at 5 kb and increased to 358 and 618 genes at 20 and 50 kb, respectively. Chromosome-stratified randomization showed that the shared 10 kb gene set overlapped pig QTL intervals more often than expected by chance (56.47% observed versus 43.23% random mean; empirical P < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: Across five breed-representative pig assemblies, we identified 23,767 paired-LTR ERV candidates, of which only 75 (0.32%) met the structural-completeness criteria, confirming that the detected porcine ERV catalog is dominated by degraded elements. Complete loci showed assembly-level variation in retroviral affinities and relative insertion-age profiles, while the five-assembly shared 10 kb ERV-proximal gene set showed non-random QTL colocalization (56.47% observed versus 43.23% random mean; empirical P < 0.0001). Benchmarking against published porcine endogenous retrovirus (PERV) and retroviral insertion polymorphism (RIP) resources linked 9 complete loci to reconstructed Sus scrofa ERV6A/B full-length ERVs (SscERV6A/B Fl-ERVs) and left 66 complete loci outside that focused set. This catalog provides concrete ERV loci and host-gene contexts for donor-line evaluation and future population-scale, T2T-informed studies of porcine ERV diversity.

papers.abstract_en: Whole-body MRI (WB-MRI) is increasingly used for early diagnosis, cancer staging and treatment monitoring, but adoption remains sub-optimal. The aim of this scoping review was to map research on patient and provider perspectives of WB-MRI in oncology, and identify methodological limitations and evidence gaps. The review followed the JBI methodological framework and the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Five electronic databases were searched from inception to 29th March 2025: Cochrane Library, PubMed, APA PsycINFO, APA Psych Articles, and Academic Search Complete. Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed by two authors independently, using COVIDENCE software, with results summarized via narrative synthesis. Twenty-eight studies met eligibility criteria, covering four distinct populations: general population (n = 8), people with cancer pre-disposition syndromes (n = 7), or suspected or confirmed cancer (n = 10), and radiologists (n = 3). Few studies examined beliefs about WB-MRI. Limited evidence shows awareness of WB-MRI attributes, such as the absence of ionising radiation, predicts preferences among cancer patients. Research on radiologists shows low levels of WB-MRI adoption in the USA and UK, attributed to limited scanner availability and a lack of trained radiologists. Among patients, uptake is modest (60%) in both population cohort studies and those recommended for surveillance, but the role of scan beliefs in predicting uptake has not been explored. Undergoing WB-MRI, or being notified of incidental findings, does not appear to cause adverse psychological consequences, but cancer specific concerns were not always assessed and research not always adequately powered. Evidence of provider and patient perspectives towards WB-MRI is limited and of varying quality. The development of validated measures examining WB-MRI beliefs and experience would enhance research and facilitate future data synthesis.Clinical trial number Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: Immunotherapy enhances antitumor immunity to eliminate malignant cells and has great potential to prevent tumor recurrence and distant metastasis. In addition to direct tumor destruction, microwave ablation (MWA) remodels the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and induces antitumor immune responses, providing a strong rationale for combination with immunotherapy. As key regulators of immune-cell trafficking and function, chemokines critically mediate the synergy between MWA and immunotherapy. In this review, we summarize the effects of MWA on the TIME, the central role of chemokine networks in this process, and recent advances in MWA-based combinatorial immunotherapy, including clinical progress. papers.abstract_en: Sex-based differences in chronic liver disease (CLD) incidence and progression are well documented, yet the mechanistic basis of this sexual disparity remains elusive. Here, leveraging a large-scale metabolomics database comprising 9,254 individuals, we identify the endogenous bile acid, isoursodeoxycholic acid (isoUDCA), as a candidate mediator of female-associated hepatoprotection. Mechanistically, isoUDCA promotes the nuclear accumulation of SREBP2. This upregulates the intracellular transporter STARD4 and its functionally coupled downstream enzyme CYP7B1, thereby facilitating intracellular cholesterol handling and metabolic conversion. Collectively, our findings support a microbiome-bile acid-liver axis that may contribute to sex differences in CLD susceptibility and support further evaluation of isoUDCA as a potential therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) comprise a group of lethal malignancies, yet developing SCC-specific therapies remains challenging, largely due to a lack of druggable targets. We identify SOX2 condensation as a shared cancer hallmark across esophageal, head and neck, and lung SCCs. Within SOX2, the activation domain 1 (AD1) acts as the condensate-promoting region via its aromatic and hydrophobic residues. Site-specific mutagenesis, orthotopic mouse models, and multi-omics sequencing demonstrate that SOX2 condensates upregulate oncogene expression by enhancing SOX2 chromatin occupancy, H3K27ac enrichment, and chromatin interactions at oncogenic loci such as FGFR2, thereby promoting SCC progression. An FDA-approved drug screen reveals that the proteasome inhibitor ixazomib disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner. Upon ixazomib treatment, the substrate-binding domain of HSP70 blocks SOX2 AD1, selectively dissolving SOX2 condensates, downregulating oncogene expression, and suppressing condensate-positive SCC patient-derived xenografts. These findings highlight targeting SOX2 condensates with proteasome inhibitors as an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is traditionally attributed to dysfunction of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, but the contribution of extra-reproductive organs remains unclear. Among CD8+ T-cell subsets, virtual memory CD8+ T (TVM) cells preferentially expand in patients and experimental models and accumulate in reproductive tissues. Mechanistically, ovarian TVM cells secrete pro-inflammatory cytokines and CCL5, thereby recruiting myeloid cells to the ovary and amplifying local inflammation. Therapeutically, JAK inhibition restricts TVM-cell differentiation, redirects CD8+ T-cell fate away from a cytotoxic CXCR3high state and ameliorates PMOS-like pathology. These findings identify TVM cells as key effectors linking androgen-induced thymic remodeling to ovarian inflammation and persistent pathology.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: As the global population continues to age, biological aging has emerged as a significant public health challenge. It is imperative to identify modifiable factors and underlying mechanisms that can promote healthy aging. Allostatic load (AL), a comprehensive indicator of chronic stress, is linked to numerous adverse outcomes in behavioral health. However, there is a paucity of comprehensive analyses and mechanistic investigations regarding the relationship between AL and biological aging across the entire population. This study seeks to elucidate the relationship between AL and biological aging, with a particular focus on examining the mediating role of the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII). METHOD: This study analyzed data from NHANES (2001-2010 and 2015-2018) with 25,775 U.S. adults, excluding those with missing data. It measured AL using 8 biomarkers and assessed biological aging with four indicators: Phenotypic Age, Biological Age, GOLD BioAge, and Light BioAge. The DII was calculated from 24-h dietary recall of 45 food items. Sociodemographic and clinical factors were covariates. Weighted linear and logistic regressions examined the complex relationship between AL, DII, and biological aging, with subgroup and mediation analyses exploring mediating role of DII in the AL-aging link. RESULT: A total of 21.56% of participants were in the high AL group, showing significantly higher DII scores and elevated biological aging indicators compared to the low AL group (P < 0.001). After adjusting for confounders, high AL was linked to faster biological aging, with a 2.08-year increase in Phenotypic Age and a 9.06-year increase in Biological Age. Odds ratios for elevated GOLD BioAge and Light BioAge were 1.60 and 2.16, respectively (P < 0.001). The AL-aging link was stronger in young/middle-aged adults, females, and non-obese individuals. DII was positively linked to all aging indicators, and exploratory mediation analysis suggested that DII may statistically account for a small proportion of the AL-aging association, with mediation proportions ranging from 0.33% to 5.45% (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: In a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults, elevated AL is significantly associated with accelerated biological aging assessed by multiple complementary indicators, and exploratory mediation analysis suggested that DII may partly account for part of this association. These findings underscore the importance of mitigating chronic physiological stress and reducing the inflammatory potential of the diet as strategies to promote healthy aging. Clinical assessment of AL and DII may provide valuable insights for identifying individuals at risk of accelerated biological aging and guiding targeted intervention measures to improve long-term health outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Experimental models and epidemiological data suggest that the maternal nutritional environment during gestation plays important roles in brain development with consequences on cognitive health. Epigenetic marks, such as methylation and histone modifications, are likely to be involved in this programming, but little addressed the impact of maternal metabolism at the preconceptional period. In mice, we recently demonstrated lasting effects of a maternal preconceptional weight loss on metabolic outcomes and behaviors related to food intake in the male offspring, exhibiting a reduction in olfactory sensitivity, along with a lack of fasting-induced olfactory-based motivation. To evaluate if this effect was driven by epigenetic modifications in the olfactory bulb, we profiled brain DNA methylation, a fundamental process in mediating the relation between early life environment and long-term behaviors in mice according to the maternal status. RESULTS: Using oxidative reduced representation bisulfite sequencing to specifically target 5mC in mice exposed to preconceptional weight loss versus controls, we identified 11,055 differentially methylated cytosines and 150 differential methylated regions (DMRs) located in 111 genes in the olfactory bulb, a main region involved in odor processing and integration. Among the cytosines differentially methylated, half were hypermethylated. Methylation remodeling according to the maternal group preferentially affected noncoding intragenic regions, distal regulatory elements, and open sea CpGs, while promoter CpG islands remain relatively resistant to modification in DNA methylome. The functional annotation of DMRs pointed out genes related to histones kinases, energy signaling, synaptic function, and cellular differentiation, suggesting that targeted methylation changes may simultaneously influence epigenetic regulation, metabolism, and neurobiology. CONCLUSION: Thanks to a single-base analysis of differential methylated CpGs, we present novel evidence that the maternal dietary environment prior to conception exerts maternally-driven epigenetic effects, markedly altering 5-methylcytosine patterns in the adult offspring brain. This long-lasting remodeling of the offspring's olfactory bulb methylome may underlie the described alterations in olfactory-driven behaviors of offspring born to WL mother.

papers.abstract_en: Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS) is a rare congenital disorder characterised by craniofacial features, growth retardation, limb anomalies, and intellectual disability. The condition arises from pathogenic variants in genes encoding cohesin complex components or regulators, most frequently NIPBL. Despite advances in genomic testing, approximately 30% of clinically diagnosed cases remain unresolved, suggesting the presence of non-coding variants. We investigated 10 classical CdLS patients negative for pathogenic variants in NIPBL, SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21, and HDAC8. Genome-wide methylation profiling was performed to identify CdLS-specific epigenetic signatures. Episignature-positive cases underwent trio-based deep sequencing of the entire NIPBL locus while targeted NIPBL RNA sequencing was used to assess splicing. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed in episignature-negative individuals. Five of ten patients exhibited a positive CdLS episignature in blood, saliva, or skin. Deep sequencing identified de novo deep intronic NIPBL variants in all cases, and two additional variants in episignature-negative patients. Seven distinct intronic variants were identified across introns 4, 10, 21, and 32. In silico tools predicted the creation or activation of cryptic splice sites in six variants. RNA sequencing confirmed pseudoexon inclusion in three patients, leading to premature termination codons and predicted nonsense-mediated decay. Tissue-specific variation in aberrant transcript expression was observed between blood and fibroblasts. We conclude that deep intronic NIPBL variants represent an under-recognised cause of CdLS, frequently escaping detection by conventional exome analysis. Integration of methylation episignatures, deep intronic sequencing, and RNA analysis enhances diagnostic yield and provides insight into the regulatory architecture of cohesinopathies.

papers.abstract_en: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is a complex three-dimensional (3D) spinal deformity. Although standing full-spine radiography remains the cornerstone of clinical diagnosis and longitudinal follow-up, two-dimensional projections cannot fully characterize vertebral rotation, local osseous geometry, or global spatial alignment. In recent years, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), conventional radiography, EOS/biplanar radiography, 3D ultrasound, and surface imaging have increasingly been integrated with deep learning, statistical shape modeling, and generative approaches, substantially expanding the technical pathways for patient-specific 3D reconstruction in AIS. However, substantial heterogeneity remains across studies with respect to input constraints, target populations, reference standards, and validation endpoints, and the evidentiary boundaries between technical performance, AIS-specific validity, and clinical validity have not been systematically clarified. This review adopted a structured methodological framework and systematically searched the Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed/MEDLINE, and IEEE Xplore, supplemented by forward and backward citation tracking. Study-level evidence was synthesized across imaging inputs, reconstruction tasks, algorithmic paradigms, and validation designs. A total of 115 core studies were included, comprising 32 AIS-specific studies (27.8%), 21 scoliosis-specific or mixed-population studies (18.3%), and 62 studies based on general spinal-image-analysis evidence (53.9%). Based on the reference standards and validation endpoints used, we established a five-level validation framework ranging from image/segmentation-level validation (L1), anatomical-structure-level validation (L2), and clinical-parameter-level validation (L3), to workflow/generalization-level validation (L4) and clinical-translation-level validation (L5). An evidence-gap matrix based on "imaging modality × methodological task" was also constructed. Among the 115 studies, 28 (24.3%) reached a maximum of L1, 49 (42.6%) reached L2, 34 (29.6%) reached L3, and only 4 (3.5%) reached L4; no study met the L5 criteria, and no explicit AIS-specific external validation was identified. Current evidence indicates that CT provides a strong basis for high-fidelity osseous reconstruction, EOS has accumulated relatively continuous AIS-specific evidence for weight-bearing 3D parameter assessment, and 3D ultrasound offers advantages for repeated radiation-free parameter measurement, whereas MRI-based reconstruction and limited-projection 3D recovery remain rapidly evolving fields. The principal challenge has therefore shifted from whether a 3D structure can be generated to whether structural fidelity can be translated into reliable clinical parameters and whether models can generalize consistently across independent AIS populations, imaging systems, and acquisition protocols. Future work should prioritize AIS-specific multicenter validation resources, task-matched 3D reference standards, and a continuous evidence chain linking structural fidelity, clinical-parameter validity, external generalization, and clinical impact, thereby advancing AIS 3D reconstruction from technical feasibility toward trustworthy clinical application.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is among the most devastating modes of progression in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although dose escalation of third-generation EGFR-TKIs has been an important central nervous system (CNS)-directed salvage strategy, therapeutic options after progression on this intensification approach remain limited. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients treated between September 2024 and December 2025. Eligible patients were adults (≥18 years) with histologically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, a documented EGFR mutation, and LM diagnosed by gadolinium-enhanced MRI or positive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology. Patients received ivonescimab plus chemotherapy after documented intracranial or extracranial progression on a dose-escalated third-generation EGFR-TKI regimen used for LM management, with or without concurrent CSF-directed therapy. Ivonescimab was given intravenously at 20 mg/kg every 3 weeks with chemotherapy selected according to prior treatment and clinical status. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and LM progression-free survival (LM-PFS). RESULTS: Of 517 screened patients, 33 initiated ivonescimab plus chemotherapy and comprised the overall treated cohort. Concurrent intrathecal or intraventricular chemotherapy was administered to 29 of 33 patients (87.9%). The median age was 61 years (IQR 56-62); 24 (72.7%) were female; 24 (72.7%) had baseline ECOG performance status of 2-3. The median number of prior therapy lines was 4 (IQR 3-6). At a median follow-up of 8.28 months, median OS was 8.54 months (95% CI 5.75-14.32), median LM-PFS was 6.54 months (95% CI 3.42-11.86), and median systemic PFS was 4.83 months (95% CI 2.79-7.56). Three-month treatment persistence was 64.4% (95% CI 44.9-78.6). Among 29 patients evaluable for LM response, 6 achieved a response, yielding an LM response rate of 20.7% (95% CI 8.0-39.7) and an LM disease control rate of 82.8% (95% CI 64.2-94.2). Among 31 patients with evaluable safety documentation, grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 14 (45.2%), most commonly hematologic toxicities. No permanent ivonescimab discontinuation due to toxicity was documented. CONCLUSIONS: This cohort provides real-world outcome data for patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and LM receiving multimodality salvage treatment incorporating ivonescimab plus chemotherapy after dose-escalated third-generation EGFR-TKI failure.

papers.abstract_en: Filamin C (FLNC) is an essential cytoskeletal protein required for cardiomyocyte structural integrity and mechanotransduction. Truncating FLNC variants cause haploinsufficiency associated with dilated and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathies, yet no therapies currently address the underlying defect of FLNC deficiency. In tamoxifen-inducible, cardiomyocyte-specific Flnc knockout mice, systemic delivery of optimized MyoAAV2A vectors restored full-length FLNC expression and re-established sarcomeric localization following cardiomyocyte FLNC depletion. FLNC replacement also attenuated pathological transcriptional remodeling and compensatory changes in cytoskeletal and junction-associated proteins. These findings demonstrate that systemic split-intein-mediated reconstitution of full-length FLNC can preserve cardiac structure and function in vivo, providing preclinical support for a mutation-independent therapeutic strategy for FLNC-associated cardiomyopathy.
