papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Perioperative 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) is a guideline-recommended standard for patients with resectable gastric cancer or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma globally. Guidance is limited on patient selection, nutritional optimization, and toxicity management within existing guidelines. This study aimed to develop an international consensus to address these management gaps. METHODS: A modified Delphi methodology, informed by the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method, was conducted virtually between March and August 2025. A multidisciplinary panel of 16 experts independently rated draft clinical statements across multiple domains. Responses were anonymized, with structured, iterative rounds of feedback and re-rating. Consensus was defined a priori as a median score of 7-9 (appropriate) or 1-3 (inappropriate) with a disagreement index ≤1.0. RESULTS: Consensus was reached on 66.3% of the statements. Experts agreed that patients aged >70 years should not be routinely excluded from perioperative FLOT but require comprehensive assessment; inclusion of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) 0-1 is appropriate, and ECOG PS 0-2 may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Adequate organ function, correction of baseline conditions, hepatitis B screening, and dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase testing are appropriate before FLOT initiation. Universal baseline nutritional screening and support, proactive intervention for malnourished patients, and structured physical activity were endorsed. Surgical planning was supported through multidisciplinary input, with defined perioperative windows, individualized dosing, and flexibility in pre-/postoperative cycles. For toxicity management, the panel supported dose modification over drug omission, where possible. CONCLUSION: This Delphi consensus provides expert-driven, practice-oriented advisories codifying fitness-based selection, nutrition-forward optimization, and pragmatic toxicity management. The resulting guidance builds on current standards and provides internationally applicable consensus statements to ultimately enhance patient care.

papers.abstract_en: Epigenetic modifications are critical determinants governing the proper initiation and progression of gametogenesis. Accumulating evidence has indicated that epigenetic dysregulation underlies the pathogenesis of infertility. However, detailed information on the individual powerful roles of these epigenetic enzymes in facilitating programmed meiosis remains elusive. This study indicates that lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) plays critical roles during meiotic prophase I in mouse spermatogenesis. Germ cell-specific deletion of the Lsd1 gene in male mice caused meiotic arrest at the pachytene stage, ultimately leading to infertility. In primary spermatocytes of Lsd1-deficient mice, compromised homologous chromosome synapsis and DNA double-strand break repair activated the DNA damage checkpoint pathway, triggering spermatocyte apoptosis. Mechanistically, LSD1 directly binds to the promoters of meiotic genes, including Prdm9 and Rpa2, to regulate their expression during meiosis. PRDM9 and RPA2 are upregulated upon LSD1 loss and are essential for homologous recombination and DNA double-strand break repair. The promoters of Prdm9 and Rpa2 are also occupied by H3K4me2, whose levels increase upon LSD1 loss. Collectively, this study highlights the crucial role of LSD1 in orchestrating meiotic genes, possibly through its demethylase activity during spermatogenesis, and may help explain the pathology of non-obstructive azoospermia in humans.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Non thrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVL) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case-control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein stenoses greater than 20 percent were included and categorized by history of left lower extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or prior venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t tests, with statistical significance defined as p<0.05. RESULTS: 45 patients were included, comprising 9 with prior DVT and 36 without. Amongst all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed left common iliac vein showed the strongest associations with a history of prior DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio (log2 fold change -1.539, p=0.007), peak velocity (log2 fold change -0.999, p=0.002), and mean velocity (log2 fold change -0.989, p=0.002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (log2 fold change 0.363, p=0.033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the left common iliac vein at the compression point was the strongest predictor of prior DVT whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSION: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Facial appearance offers a non-invasive window into health. We built Foundation Artificial Intelligence for Health Recognition-Face (FAHR-Face), a foundation model trained on more than 40 million facial photographs and fine-tuned it for two distinct tasks: biological age estimation (FAHR-FaceAge) and survival prediction (FAHR-FaceSurvival). METHODS: FAHR-FaceAge underwent two-stage, age-balanced fine-tuning on ten public image datasets; FAHR-FaceSurvival was fine-tuned on 34 363 photographs of patients with cancer. Model robustness (cosmetic surgery, make-up, pose, and lighting) and independence (attention mapping) were tested. Both models were clinically tested in two independent cancer patient datasets with survival analysed by multivariate Cox models and adjusted for clinical prognostic factors. FINDINGS: For age estimation, FAHR-FaceAge had the lowest mean absolute error of 5·1 years on public datasets, outperforming benchmark models and maintaining accuracy across the full human lifespan. In patients with cancer, FAHR-FaceAge outperformed a previous age estimation model in survival prognostication. FAHR-FaceSurvival showed robust prediction of mortality, and the highest-risk quartile had more than triple the mortality of the lowest (adjusted hazard ratio 3·23; p<0·0001). These findings were validated in the independent cohort and both models showed generalisability across age, sex, race, and cancer subgroups. The two algorithms provided distinct, complementary prognostic information; attention mapping revealed that each model relied on distinct facial regions. The combination of FAHR-FaceAge and FAHR-FaceSurvival improved prognostic accuracy. INTERPRETATION: A single foundation model can generate inexpensive, scalable facial biomarkers that capture both biological ageing and disease-related mortality risk. The foundation model enabled effective training by use of relatively small clinical datasets. Routine quantitative facial analysis could enhance risk stratification when traditional biomarkers are unavailable. FUNDING: EU European Research Council.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The growing threat to health systems posed by extreme weather events (EWEs) disproportionately affects people living with HIV and tuberculosis disease in high-burden, low-resource settings. In Zimbabwe, for example, the 2023-24 El Niño-induced drought intensified food insecurity and reduced access to clinics and medication for such vulnerable populations. We aimed to conduct a formative evaluation to assess the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery and identify potential climate-adaptive health-service strategies. METHODS: In this survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study with a formative evaluation supplemented by qualitative data, we surveyed people living with HIV from Sept 19 to Dec 19, 2024, across 321 clinics in Zimbabwe to describe their perceived impact of EWEs on their health. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. The inclusion criteria were being diagnosed with HIV, being older than 18 years, and receiving HIV care at Organization for Public Health Interventions and Development (OPHID) clinics during the study period. Individuals who were not receiving HIV care at an OPHID clinic or who were younger than 18 years were excluded. A client satisfaction survey was used to collect data from in-person surveys. The survey included questions related to the general effects of EWEs, such as drought, extreme heat, and flooding; how EWEs had affected HIV or tuberculosis care; and what, if any, services were currently available or should be made available to mitigate climate impacts on health. We also conducted six focus group discussions (FGDs; five to eight participants per group) between March 12 and May 12, 2024, across the Bulilima, Mangwe, and Matobo districts. We used a convenience sampling approach to select patients who had visited the health facility for medical check-ups, medication resupply, or viral load testing, as recorded in clinical registers and verified by clinical staff. Eligible participants for the FGDs were adults (≥18 years) with HIV, or with current or previous tuberculosis treatment, receiving care at the study facility during the recruitment period; those under 18 years or not receiving care at the facility were excluded. Participants' sex was self-reported at enrolment. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, whereas FGD data were analysed using a modified framework approach. The main outcomes were the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery outcomes, as reported by affected communities, and community-prioritised mitigation strategies to feasibly address climate-sensitive determinants and barriers to care. FINDINGS: Among 1804 eligible participants approached across 15 districts, all completed the survey and were included in the analysis. Most survey participants (1363 [75·6%] of 1804 participants) reported noticing changes in climate over the past 5 years; of these 1363 participants, 900 (66·0%) were female and 1024 (75·1%) participants reported disruptions to their HIV care during the time they noticed changes in climate. Survey respondents reported that climate-related disruptions were associated with increased food insecurity (reported by 877 [85·6%] of 1024 participants) and water shortage (667 [65·1%] of 1024 participants). Qualitative analysis confirmed that the barriers to HIV and tuberculosis care from EWEs included widespread food insecurity, crop failures, and livestock deaths, with consequent effects on income leading to challenges in paying for food and transportation to clinics. Participants highlighted the need for expanded services that facilitate social and economic wellbeing, including nutrition support, water access, transportation, and income-generating activities, and decentralised models of health-care delivery. INTERPRETATION: Extreme heat and drought affect food and water security and have financial implications, creating challenges for patients to access care in Zimbabwe. Our findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, climate-adaptive strategies to maintain HIV and tuberculosis care in such climate-vulnerable regions. FUNDING: Nina Ireland Program in Lung Health.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sexual violence against women is a major public health problem in Latin America, yet evidence on its social determinants is scarce and often conflates partner and non-partner forms. We characterised determinants of intimate partner sexual violence (IPSV), non-partner sexual assault (NPSA), and non-partner sexual harassment (NPSH) in Chile and compared their risk profiles. METHODS: We analysed pooled 2017 and 2020 rounds of the Chilean National Survey on Violence in the Family and Other Settings, representative of urban women aged 15 years or older; fieldwork preceded Chile's first COVID-19 case. We fitted multilevel logistic regression for past-year outcomes, women nested in municipalities. FINDINGS: The sample comprised 13,128 women (8335 for IPSV models). Past-year prevalence was 2.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.4-3.3) for IPSV, 2.5% (2.1-3.0) for NPSA, and 11.3% (10.4-12.3) for NPSH. IPSV was associated with relational factors: dominant relationship (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 6.40, 4.68-8.76) and partner violence elsewhere (2.79, 1.75-4.43); between-municipality variance was negligible. NPSA and NPSH concentrated in younger women and the Metropolitan Region (OR 2.92 [2.00-4.28] and 2.29 [1.77-2.96]); both were associated with social participation (1.49 [1.11-2.00] and 1.26 [1.09-1.46]). Childhood sexual abuse was associated with all three (OR 2.05 [1.45-2.89], 3.03 [2.20-4.20], and 2.06 [1.72-2.46]). Reported non-partner victimisation rose between 2017 and 2020, pre-pandemic. INTERPRETATION: Risk profiles differed: relational and life-course for IPSV, age-graded and metropolitan for NPSA and NPSH; childhood sexual abuse was common to all three, supporting trauma-informed responses. FUNDING: Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo, Chile (Doctoral Scholarship 21212141).

papers.abstract_en: Metastasis is the primary cause of mortality in cancer including lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Preferentially expressed antigen of melanoma (PRAME), a cancer-testis antigen, displays context-dependent functions across malignancies, but its biological role in LUAD metastasis has not been clearly defined. Here, we demonstrate that the significantly upregulated PRAME in metastatic LUAD directly interacts with the m6A methyltransferase METTL3 and promotes its K63-linked non-proteolytic ubiquitination. This modification occurs at lysine 235 of METTL3, increases its protein stability and facilitates METTL3 interaction with METTL14 and WTAP. Consequently, m6A modification of TGFB2 mRNA and activation of the TGF-β signaling pathway are enhanced, which is essential for PRAME-driven pro-metastatic effects both in vitro and in vivo. Clinically, PRAME expression positively correlates with METTL3 protein abundance and TGF-β pathway activation, and is robustly associated with poor clinical outcomes. Taken together, our findings identify K63-linked ubiquitination as a previously unrecognized post-translational modification of METTL3 and underscore the importance of the PRAME/METTL3/TGF-β axis in LUAD metastasis, providing mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for this malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: Cognitive and motor dysfunction occurs in 30%-50% of people with HIV/AIDS. Within this clinical spectrum, HIV-associated ataxia is an uncommon but debilitating disorder with poorly defined neuropathological mechanisms. This study investigated two rhesus macaques with chronic simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infection that developed progressive ataxia, characterized by postural imbalance and nystagmus. Comparative neuropathological profiling of cerebellar tissue from ataxic SIV-infected macaques, non-ataxic SIV-infected macaques, and uninfected controls revealed that ataxia was associated with diffuse cerebellar atrophy, disrupted tissue organization, Purkinje cell degeneration, demyelination, glial nodule formation, and prominent microglial neuroinflammation. Cerebellar infection with simian polyomavirus 40 (SV40), a member of the Polyomaviridae family, was identified as the cause of the lesions, with viral tropism primarily involving cerebellar granule neurons. Mechanistically, SV40 infection induced neuronal pyroptosis and inflammatory cytokine release, promoting microglial recruitment and activation, amplifying local neuroinflammation, and culminating in nodular aggregate formation. Collectively, these findings establish SV40 infection as a direct driver of cerebellar pathology in SIV-associated ataxia and define a pathogenic sequence linking granule neuron pyroptosis, microglial activation, and progressive cerebellar injury-a cascade that may parallel polyomavirus-induced ataxia in people living with HIV-1.

papers.abstract_en: Tuft cells are specialized chemosensory epithelial cells that contribute to mucosal immunity, yet how their differentiation is regulated in human airway disease remains unclear. Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps(CRSwNP) features type 2 inflammation and expansion of sinonasal tuft cells, consistent with type 2 cytokine-driven epithelial remodeling. Using primary human sinonasal epithelial air-liquid interface cultures, we examined tuft cell differentiation across disease phenotypes. IL-13-induced expansion of POU2F3+ tuft cells and generated a BMX+ subset consistent with a mature or activated phenotype. These IL-13 activated cultures exhibited enhanced responsiveness to chemosensory ligands such as succinate and denatonium, indicating functional activation. Surprisingly, IL-13-driven sinonasal tuft cell differentiation occurred despite inhibition of STAT6 and ERK signaling, suggesting involvement of noncanonical pathways. Retinoic acid(RA) emerged as a selective regulator of tuft cell differentiation specifically in CRSwNP. RA did not alter STAT6 phosphorylation or canonical IL-13-responsive gene expression, indicating that RA suppresses tuft cell differentiation through distinct mechanisms. These findings highlight a noncanonical pathway of IL-13-mediated tuft cell expansion and identify retinoic acid as a context-dependent regulator of tuft cell differentiation in the airway. These findings demonstrate methods to regulate human sinonasal tuft cell differentiation across disease phenotypes, opening avenues for tuft cell-targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: H2AK119ub (H2Aub) and H3K27me3, which are deposited by the Polycomb group (PcG) complexes PRC1 and PRC2, respectively, cooperatively repress developmental genes. However, in human preimplantation embryos, H3K27me3 undergoes genome-wide erasure and subsequent restoration. How H3K27me3 is reestablished and whether PcG complexes still regulate gene repression in human embryos remain unknown. Here, we profiled H2Aub dynamics from human gametes to blastocysts. H2Aub emerges in GC-rich regions as early as the two-cell stage, progressively accumulates at both active and inactive genes, and further culminates at PcG targets in later stages. H3K27me3 is weakly correlated with H2Aub in oocytes and two-cell embryos but colocalizes with H2Aub at H3K4me3-depleted, inactive PcG targets in blastocysts. Loss of H2Aub abolishes H3K27me3 reestablishment at PcG targets causing moderate derepression, accompanied by ectopic H3K27me3 deposition and impaired embryonic development. Finally, H2Aub and DNA methylation cooperatively maintain H3K27me3 patterning in human embryonic stem cells. Therefore, H2Aub-dependent H3K27me3 deposition underlies the earliest establishment of Polycomb repression in humans.

papers.abstract_en: Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) enables gentle, rapid and efficient volumetric imaging of biological specimens. Despite its potential, LSFM has fragmented into multiple variants, each narrowly optimized for specific samples or imaging regimes, limiting its broad applicability. Here we introduce the multi-immersion oblique plane microscope (miOPM), an adaptable LSFM platform for high-resolution imaging ranging from subcellular dynamics to whole organisms and cleared tissues. miOPM supports seamless interchangeability of oil, water and air objectives and maintains diffraction-limited performance across a refractive index range of 1.33 to 1.51. It is compatible with standard sample mounting, current clearing protocols and high-throughput 3D imaging. We leverage miOPM to image diverse biological specimens at multiple spatial scales. By expanding the adaptability and ease of use of LSFM, miOPM is poised to democratize advanced 3D imaging.

Here we identify the G-protein-coupled receptor, Rsd1, as a farnesol-responsive sensor controlling this dormancy switch in the plant pathogen Fusarium pseudograminearum, which causes Fusarium crown rot. Under high population density and nutrient limitation, endogenous farnesol activates Rsd1 and downstream signalling pathways to suppress conidial germination. Rsd1 also responds to extracellular farnesol, linking environmental signals to an intrinsic transcriptional programme for dormancy. This adaptive response enhances survival but creates a fitness trade-off during plant infection. Specific rhizosphere-associated bacteria also contribute by promoting or inhibiting germination of dormant conidia through farnesol-Rsd1 sensing. Consortia assembled from these bacteria altered the balance between stress-resilient dormancy and infection-associated germination, thereby modulating disease severity. Our findings demonstrate how microbial interactions reshape intrinsic fungal regulatory programmes governing dormancy and infection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the management of bezoar ileus in patients who have already undergone abdominal surgery is limited. We reviewed conservative and surgical pathways in clinically selected patients, with particular attention to patient selection criteria and how each pathway was defined. METHODS: We reviewed 80 patients with CT-confirmed bezoar ileus and previous abdominal surgery who were treated between January 2010 and December 2021. Twenty-six completed conservative treatment, and 54 underwent surgery. In practice, conservative treatment was used for clinically stable patients without peritonitis or CT signs suggesting ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, provided that close clinical monitoring was possible. Conservative treatment included bowel rest, intravenous fluids, electrolyte correction, symptom-directed medication and nasogastric decompression when needed. Failure was defined by clinical deterioration, persistent or worsening obstruction, inability to tolerate oral intake, or new radiological concern. The primary outcome was clinical resolution during the index admission. Secondary outcomes were hospitalisation, in-hospital mortality, postoperative complications and readmission after discharge. RESULTS: The treatment groups were not equivalent at baseline. Patients treated surgically more often had gastric bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 0/26, p = 0.002), multiple bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 1/26, 3.8%, p = 0.009) and greater small-bowel dilatation (median 4.0 cm vs. 3.4 cm, p = 0.014). All 26 patients in the conservative pathway completed the index admission without operation, although routine radiological confirmation of resolution was not performed. Median hospitalisation was 4 days (IQR 4-5) in the surgical group and 7 days (6-8) in the conservative group (p < 0.001); this difference should be interpreted in the context of clinical selection and local practice. Postoperative complications occurred in 11/54 surgical patients (20.4%), including two deaths from pulmonary embolism. Among discharged patients, readmission did not differ significantly between groups (13/52, 25.0% after surgery vs. 5/26, 19.2% after conservative treatment; p = 0.776). Exploratory regression findings were treated as hypothesis-generating only. CONCLUSIONS: Conservative treatment may be feasible in selected stable patients with bezoar ileus after previous abdominal surgery. Surgery remains appropriate for patients with peritonitis, suspected ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, clinical deterioration, or failure of conservative management. Because treatment was not protocolised and the groups differed at baseline, the findings should be read as observational and hypothesis-generating, not as evidence that either strategy is superior.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To explore needs among persons with advanced COPD and informal caregivers, and to explore how palliative care can address those needs. BACKGROUND: COPD is a common, progressive disease affecting lung function and represents a leading cause of death. Advanced COPD is associated with a high symptom burden and poor quality of life. Persons with advanced COPD may benefit from palliative care, but its use among persons with COPD remains limited, also in Germany. METHODS: A qualitative, multi-perspective interview study was conducted with persons suffering from advanced COPD, informal caregivers, and formal caregivers (general practitioners, pulmonologists, and palliative care physicians). A total of 53 interviews were analysed following structuring (Kuckartz') as well as latent content analysis methods using MAXQDA. RESULTS: Key needs were identified in the following domains (1) management of dyspnoea and anxiety, (2) home-based healthcare, (3) emergency planning and support, (4) psychosocial care, (5) organisational support, and (6) timely information about COPD and palliative care. Persons who had previously received PC reported various needs met in the first five areas. CONCLUSIONS: Persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers reported numerous needs. Persons receiving palliative care reported relief from various needs. Timely information about COPD's progression and palliative care could increase acceptance and thus use of palliative care among these persons and could consequently reduce or curtail the burden of living with advanced COPD.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: Using more than five decades of national data, we examine how age, period and cohort factors influence lung cancer mortality in Switzerland, and forecast future death counts to the early 2040s. METHODS: Lung cancer deaths were extracted from Swiss vital statistics. We applied age-period-cohort (APC) modelling to lung cancer mortality rates using substantiated assumptions about the age-mortality relationship as model constraints. To account for the uncertainty in the age-mortality relationship, boundary constraints were applied to the line of APC solutions, yielding a range of plausible results. In an alternative model, we replaced the cohort terms with smoking prevalence estimates from Swiss health surveys, enabling unconstrained modelling of age and period effects. Predictions are based on modelled age trends, and linearly extrapolated period and cohort trends. RESULTS: Plausible age, period and cohort effects indicated that age-specific mortality risks decline at the oldest ages, that period effects were minimal, while cohort effects showed distinct peak risks for men born around 1909 and women born around 1954. Among women, birth cohorts with the highest mortality closely aligned with those exhibiting the highest smoking prevalence. The models predicted a decline in the number of lung cancer deaths among men beginning in the mid-2020s, and among women from the mid-2030s onwards. CONCLUSIONS: This population-based analysis of lung cancer mortality not only highlights declining mortality rates in men of all ages, but reveals an emerging downward trend among younger women. We predict that the total number of lung cancer deaths in women will begin to decrease by the mid-2030s.

papers.abstract_en: Medical image segmentation is essential for computer-aided diagnosis and precision medicine, yet conventional supervised models depend heavily on high-quality annotations and often generalize poorly across domains. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) family offers a transferable, interactive, and extensible foundation for segmentation, but direct medical transfer remains limited by domain gaps, insufficient modeling of medical semantics and anatomy, and mismatches in high-dimensional volumetric and sequential imaging scenarios. This review critically examines the evolution and native capability boundaries of SAM, SAM 2, and SAM 3. Across generations, native capabilities expand from spatial prompting to sequential propagation and concept-level target specification, without automatically conferring medical expertise. We organize medical adaptation from three connected perspectives: model adaptation and strategy selection, task knowledge organization and utilization, and application-oriented adaptation. Cross-method analysis shows that no strategy is universally optimal; effectiveness depends on the gap between foundation-model capabilities and target-task requirements, together with data scale, domain discrepancy, imaging dimensionality, computational resources, and clinical constraints. We further identify four priorities for clinical translation: standardized evaluation for cross-study comparability, controlled continual adaptation under clinical domain drift, dynamic resource scheduling for high-dimensional and real-time workflows, and uncertainty stratification and clinical reliability control. Overall, further progress depends on accurate capability assessment, condition-matched adaptation, and explicit control of computational and prediction risks.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in patients with HCC. METHODS: 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics. CONCLUSION: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

However, the relationship between CMD and the extracellular volume fraction (ECV) in patients with ischemia with no obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA) who are late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-negative remains undetermined. We used T1 mapping and ECV to assess diffuse myocardial tissue abnormalities and extracellular compartment expansion in LGE-negative patients with CMD. We then investigated how these markers correlate with global myocardial flow reserve (MFR). METHODS: Between August 2024 and May 2026, we prospectively enrolled 86 LGE-negative patients with INOCA from a single center who underwent a positron emission tomography-magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MRI) protocol. Patients with significant epicardial stenosis (stenosis on coronary angiogram or computed tomography ≥ 50%), prior history of revascularization, known myocardial infarction, or heart failure were excluded. MFR and ECV were derived from PET perfusion imaging and pre- and post-T1 mapping, respectively. CMD was defined as PET-derived MFR of < 2.0 in at least one major coronary artery territory. RESULTS: Among the 86 patients included, 39 (45.3%) were diagnosed with CMD. ECV was substantially higher in the CMD group (31.22 [29.93, 33.25]% vs. 26.66 [25.85, 27.55]%, P < 0.001), with a more modest but statistically significant elevation in native T1 (1225 ± 25 ms vs. 1212 ± 21 ms, P = 0.012). Multivariable linear regression revealed that only global MFR (β [95% confidence interval] = - 1.905 [- 2.489, - 1.321], P < 0.001) was an independent predictor of ECV in LGE-negative CMD patients. In the overall cohort, resting myocardial blood flow (MBF) (r = 0.539, P < 0.001) and global MFR (r = - 0.741, P < 0.001) were positively and negatively correlated with ECV, respectively. When participants were stratified into ECV tertiles, global MFR showed a progressive decrease (2.92 vs. 2.48 vs. 1.78; P < 0.001 for trend) with increasing ECV values. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with INOCA with CMD, prolonged native T1 and elevated ECV indicate diffuse interstitial expansion, consistent with early tissue remodeling, even when LGE is absent on CMR. These findings suggest that native T1 and ECV may hold promise as adjunctive tissue markers to support risk stratification, though their role in clinical management requires further validation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) are associated with substantial short term mortality and healthcare utilization, yet the prognostic utility of the immunonutrition based hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score in this setting remains unclear, particularly in comparison with the well validated dyspnoea, eosinopenia, consolidation, acidaemia, atrial fibrillation (DECAF) score. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single centre observational cohort study of adults presenting to the emergency department (ED) with AECOPD between June 2022 and June 2025. DECAF and HALP scores were calculated at admission using routinely collected clinical and laboratory data, and the primary outcome was 30 day in hospital mortality. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with Youden-derived, data-driven cut-off values, and we further evaluated previously validated DECAF thresholds and a categorical DECAF model. Associations with 30 day mortality were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for baseline clinical variables. Model calibration was evaluated using Brier scores and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and 30 day survival was analysed with Kaplan-Meier. RESULTS: A total of 499 patients were included in the study, 63 (12.6%) died within 30 days, and 76% of the cohort were male. The HALP score showed acceptable predictive performance (area under the curve (AUC) 0.724), at a cut-off of 16.84, sensitivity was 57.1%, specificity 75.0% and negative predictive value (NPV) 92.4% for 30 day in hospital mortality. The DECAF score demonstrated excellent discrimination for 30 day in hospital mortality (AUC 0.932), and showed significantly better discrimination than HALP (DeLong p < 0.001), using a cut-off of ≥ 4, sensitivity was 76.2%, specificity 95.6% and NPV 96.5%. CONCLUSION: In ED patients with AECOPD, the HALP score provides only limited prognostic information for 30 day in hospital mortality, whereas the DECAF score exhibits excellent discriminative performance and retains its value as a robust, clinically applicable predictor of short term outcomes in acute care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The impact of different inguinal hernia repair techniques on testicular perfusion remains a subject of clinical interest. While open and laparoscopic approaches demonstrate comparable outcomes in terms of recurrence and complications, their effects on testicular microcirculation are not fully elucidated. METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study included 180 male patients who underwent unilateral primary inguinal hernia repair using open Lichtenstein, total extraperitoneal (TEP), or transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) techniques between January 2015 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Doppler ultrasonography parameters, including resistive index (RI), peak systolic velocity (PSV), end-diastolic velocity (EDV), and testicular volume, were evaluated preoperatively, at postoperative day 7, and at 1 month. Changes over time and between groups were analyzed using multivariable regression and linear mixed-effects models. Subclinical testicular ischemia was defined based on predefined Doppler criteria. RESULTS: Early postoperative changes in testicular perfusion parameters differed significantly between surgical techniques. At postoperative day 7, RI values were higher and EDV values were lower in the Lichtenstein group compared to TEP and TAPP (p < 0.001 and p = 0.002, respectively). These differences decreased at 1 month but remained statistically significant for RI (p = 0.003). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that surgical technique, operative time, and hernia sac size were independently associated with changes in RI. Subclinical testicular ischemia was more frequent in the Lichtenstein group, while laparoscopic approaches were associated with lower odds (TEP: OR 0.34, p = 0.002; TAPP: OR 0.41, p = 0.006). Longitudinal analysis confirmed a significant time-by-technique interaction for RI (p < 0.001), indicating partial recovery over time. CONCLUSION: Surgical technique is associated with transient alterations in testicular perfusion following inguinal hernia repair. Open Lichtenstein repair demonstrated more pronounced early microvascular changes, whereas laparoscopic techniques exhibited a more stable perfusion profile. These findings highlight the importance of surgical technique and intraoperative handling in preserving testicular microcirculation.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate the nationwide adoption of genicular artery embolization (GAE) in Germany and to describe patient selection, technique, safety and radiation dose. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed procedures recorded in the quality-assurance registry of the German Society for Interventional Radiology and Minimally Invasive Therapy (DeGIR), from January 2024 to December 2025. Technical success, entered per procedure, was defined as subjective adequate devascularization of the synovial blush. Complications were graded using the modified CIRSE classification, and radiation exposure was expressed as dose-area product (DAP) and fluoroscopy time. The analysis was primarily descriptive. RESULTS: Overall, 2335 procedures in 2209 patients across 109 centers in 15 federal states were recorded (median age 67 years, IQR 59-77; 57% female; prior total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in 300, 13%). Annual volume rose from 579 procedures in 2024 to 1,756 in 2025, and the embolic agent shifted from permanent (40-21%) toward temporary microspheres (4-29%). Center-reported technical success was 93% (87% in 2024, 94% in 2025). Eleven complications were recorded (0.5%), all CIRSE grade 1-3, with no permanent sequelae; none were recorded in 2024. Median DAP was 1536 cGy cm2 (IQR 731-3048) and median fluoroscopy time 24 min (IQR 16-34). CONCLUSION: During rapid nationwide adoption, GAE was performed for osteoarthritis-related and post-TKA pain with low radiation dose and high center-reported technical success across centers of all volumes, supporting its feasibility in routine practice. The complication rate is a lower limit, as the registry is not designed for complication surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To compare the costs of percutaneous segmentectomy, a single-session combination of transarterial embolisation and microwave ablation, against chemoembolisation and radioembolisation for hepatocellular carcinoma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cost analysis of 66 patients treated with percutaneous segmentectomy at five Italian centres, using bottom-up micro-costing. Comparator costs were derived from published Italian per-session costs multiplied by mean sessions per patient, and survival from published curves. A partitioned survival model estimated life-years and incremental net monetary benefit at 50,000 euros per life-year. RESULTS: Procedural cost per treated patient was 6331 euros for percutaneous segmentectomy, 9792 euros for chemoembolisation (mean 2.94 sessions), and 21,673 euros for radioembolisation (1.52 sessions). At 24 months, percutaneous segmentectomy had lower total cost and a small life-year deficit (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio approximately 70,800 euros per life-year versus chemoembolisation and 57,500 versus radioembolisation, both above threshold). This life-year-adjusted advantage reversed versus chemoembolisation, and became neutral versus radioembolisation, in a worst-case sensitivity analysis, and reversed against both when transplantation costs for the eight transplanted patients (19%) were attributed to percutaneous segmentectomy alone. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, percutaneous segmentectomy appeared to have a lower procedural cost per treated patient than chemoembolisation and radioembolisation, mainly because it is delivered in a single session. However, because costing routes, cohorts, and survival sources were not equivalent and the life-year-adjusted comparison was not robust, no formal cost superiority can be established. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective, matched studies. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Retrospective Cohort Study with Historical Comparators.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Non-invasive tests (NITs) accurately detect fibrosis and may reduce the need for liver biopsy (LB). Detection of advanced fibrosis (≥F3) is clinically important for prognosis, but few studies have explored the use of NITs in patients with Wilson Disease (WD). METHODS: In this multicentre observational study, adult and pediatric WD patients from seven international expert centers with histologic fibrosis staging were included. NITs (Transient elastography (TE), Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), AST to platelet-ratio (APRI), Steatosis-associated fibrosis estimator (SAFE), and NAFLD fibrosis score (NFS)) and clinical data were collected. NITs were compared with liver biopsy (LB) to detect advanced fibrosis (≥F3). RESULTS: In total, 123 patients were included: median age was 30 years (IQR 17.4, 43.1); time from WD diagnosis to LB was 6.7 months (0.7, 144.1); 30.9% had advanced fibrosis (≥F3), while concomitant metabolic risk factors (obesity and diabetes) were rare. Overall, 64 patients had NITs measured within 1 year of the LB and constituted the primary analysis group. All NITs, except FIB-4, were significantly elevated in patients with ≥F3. TE had the best overall accuracy (AUC=0.79), and performed well at an optimized cut-off of ≥8.35 kPa (sens=0.88, spec=0.85). APRI had lower accuracy, but effectively ruled out ≥F3 at the optimized cut-off of ≥1.3 (AUC=0.71, sens=0.38, spec=1.00). Combining those into a score (APRITE) achieved an AUC of 0.88. DISCUSSION: TE demonstrated good diagnostic performance for identifying advanced fibrosis in WD. APRI showed high specificity, while the exploratory APRITE score showed encouraging performance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is a substantial comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to assess alterations in effective connectivity (EC) in patients with COPD and investigate their relationships with clinical measures. METHODS: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) was performed in 38 patients with COPD and 30 healthy controls. EC was estimated using vector autoregressive (VAR) modelling combined with Granger causality analysis across 26 prespecified brain regions of interest derived from our previous functional connectivity study of the same cohort. Between-group differences in directed connectivity were assessed using Welch's t-tests. Associations between EC measures showing between-group differences and clinical measures were evaluated using age-adjusted partial Pearson correlations. RESULTS: At the nominal two-sided p < 0.05 level, 37 directed connections showed between-group differences in effective connectivity, and the mean vector autoregressive coefficients for 35 of these connections lay on opposite sides of zero between the COPD and control groups. Among the connections showing between-group differences, age-adjusted associations in patients with COPD involved pulmonary function, systemic oxygenation, cognition, affect, and health status. These associations involved distributed cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions, with several directed connections showing convergence across multiple clinical domains. CONCLUSION: Resting-state VAR-based EC revealed distributed between-group differences in direction-sensitive BOLD temporal organization in COPD. Several of these EC measures were associated with pulmonary function, SpO2, respiratory and COPD symptom burden, cognition, affect, and health status after age adjustment. These findings extend the functional connectivity profile of COPD by linking directed temporal relationships to its multidimensional clinical burden.

papers.abstract_en: Benchmarks labelled by panels of human readers underpin most medical image analysis. We ask whether such a dataset has a single attainable ceiling. All 1319 annotation files of the Lung Image Database Consortium image collection (LIDC-IDRI) were parsed into 7034 reader-level ratings. Modelling each nodule by a latent malignancy propensity of which the four reader verdicts are conditionally independent draws, we prove that no image-based model can exceed, against a reader-derived label, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the propensity itself; we derive how that bound depends on the labelling policy, test the independence assumption against a prediction the fit does not use, simulate its failures, and audit a purposive sample of 22 published studies against the rules they declare. Among 905 nodules read by all four radiologists, all four agreed exactly for 11.7% and 58.0% carried ratings spanning two or more points. Across three latent families, retaining every nodule the ceiling is 0.898-0.913; discarding the 19.6% the readers split two-two lifts it to 0.946-0.954; retaining only unanimous nodules discards 57.7% and lifts it to 0.991-0.994. On the binary scale, no family predicted more reader agreement than observed; simulated reader heterogeneity would make these ceilings slightly low. Of 27 reported figures, 11 lie above the bound implied by the study's own declared rule, four beyond sampling error and two if modest heterogeneity is also allowed for. The ceiling is set by the label, not by the images.

papers.abstract_en: Measuring individual muscles and their fatty infiltration on Dixon MRI can support sarcopenia assessment, but manual annotation is time-consuming and annotated datasets are often small. This study investigated accurate individual-muscle segmentation with limited labelled data. Three datasets were used: an abdominal CT dataset of 300 subjects with adipose-tissue labels, a lower-limb Dixon MRI dataset of 25 subjects with 13 thigh and 9 calf muscles, and an independent cohort of 66 subjects for external testing. Network architecture, encoder pretraining, a Dixon-derived fat-fraction input, and a shared CT-MRI encoder were compared. A 2.5D model, subject-level cross-validation, zero-shot transfer, label-free domain adaptation, and few-shot adaptation were also evaluated. The best models reached Dice 0.947 ± 0.017  for CT adipose tissue and 0.925 ± 0.010  for thigh muscle; the best 2.5D model reached 0.928, while a reported 3D Attention-Res-V-Net reached 0.857 under a different protocol. Encoder pretraining helped most at the smallest budgets, with ImageNet performing best and comparably to CT-based pretraining at eight subjects. A shared CT-MRI encoder retained accuracy with 44 %  fewer parameters, and thigh-muscle volumes agreed closely with reference measurements (ICC ( 2 , 1 ) = 0.998  ). On the external cohort, fine-tuning raised Dice from 0.11 zero-shot to 0.61, 0.76, and 0.88 with four, eight, and 46 labelled target subjects. The fat-fraction input improved segmentation only when very few subjects (two or four) were labelled. Encoder pretraining and efficient model sharing help when annotated MRI data are scarce. A small amount of target-domain annotation substantially improves cross-cohort transfer, and repeated subject-level validation is important for reliable evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is associated with high mortality and morbidity. Antenatal counselling enables parents to prepare for the postnatal outcomes and relies on effective prognostic tools. Ultrasound (USS) predictors including observed/expected lung head ratio (o/e LHR) and liver position, are used independently, or combined into severity classifications. The aim was to evaluate the association between USS predictors, and severity classifications with survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) requirement in prenatally diagnosed CDH at Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital (BWC). METHODS: CDH patients from BWC with dates of birth between 1st December 2013-1st December 2023 were retrospectively collected. Study inclusion required o/e LHR measurement between 22- and 32-weeks gestational age (GA.) Comparisons between groups was assessed by Fisher exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Logistic regression was performed to determine prognostic ability, with area under curve (AUC) calculated. RESULTS: 91 eligible patients were identified, which included 82 left-sided, and 9 right-sided CDH. Overall, 55% survived to discharge and 13% required ECMO. In the left CDH cohort, 57% of infants survived to discharge, and 15% required ECMO. O/e LHR, liver position and the combined predictive model including o/e LHR and liver position were predictive of survival to discharge with good prognostic ability (AUC 0.769, AUC 0.703, and AUC 0.823, respectively). O/e LHR, liver position, and the combined predictive model were not predictive of ECMO requirement. In the right CDH patients, 33% survived to discharge, O/e LHR and liver position were not predictive of survival to discharge. CONCLUSION: O/e LHR, liver position and the combination of these predictors, predicted survival to discharge in prenatally diagnosed left CDH with the combined model, the most predictive particularly in the isolated left CDH sub-group. Further analysis into effective predictors for ECMO requirement, and for right and complex left CDH is required.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brain metastases (BM) are frequent in EGFR-mutated (EGFRm) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and remain challenging after prior EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This exploratory study evaluated high-dose fimmonertinib and explored subtype-specific spatial biology. METHODS: iFORCE was a prospective, single-center, single-arm study. Eligible patients had advanced NSCLC harboring EGFR mutations with previously treated BM following EGFR-TKI therapy, or intracranial disease progression. Patients received 160 mg firmonertinib once daily. The primary endpoint was intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS). Archival paired primary tumors and BM specimens from an independent retrospective cohort underwent exploratory digital spatial profiling (DSP). RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 19.7 months (95% CI, 14.5-25.3), median iPFS was 14.6 months (95% CI, 4.2-not estimable [NE]), with 12- and 18-month iPFS rates of 53.8% and 46.1%, respectively. Based on the best intracranial overall response, intracranial objective response and disease control rates were 34.8% (95% CI, 16.4-57.3) and 91.3% (95% CI, 72.0-98.9). Median systemic PFS was 10.7 months (95% CI, 3.9-NE). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 13 (56.5%) patients, mostly grade 1; one patient (4.3%) developed grade 3 stomatitis. No treatment discontinuations or treatment-related deaths were observed. DSP revealed distinct EGFR subtype-specific BM ecosystems: exon 19 deletion tumors retained immune-enriched inflammatory programs, whereas L858R-mutated tumors showed tumor-intrinsic cell-cycle, DNA-repair, RNA-splicing, apoptosis-resistance, and immune-evasion features. CONCLUSIONS: Fimonertinib 160 mg showed promising intracranial activity with a manageable safety profile in EGFR-TKI-treated EGFRm NSCLC with BM. L858R BM displayed tumor-intrinsic, microenvironment-independent biology, suggesting preferential sensitivity to high-dose firmonertinib.

While tobacco smoking is a well-established risk factor for lung cancer,the association between cannabis use and lung cancer risk remains unclear and controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis of existing observational studies aimed to evaluate the potential relationship between marijuana use and the risk ofdeveloping lung cancer. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus to identify cohort and case-controlstudies up to September 2025. Studies were selected, relevant data were extracted, and statistically analyzed using effect sizes (ES)and 95% confidence intervals (CI). All analyses were conducted using STATA software. FINDINGS: This meta-analysis included six observational studies, comprising 16 effect sizes, consisting of two cohort studies andfour case-control studies. The pooled analysis of the cohort studies (7 effect sizes) indicated a statistically significant associationbetween marijuana (cannabis) smoking and increased lung cancer risk (ES: 2.06; 95% CI: [1.04-4.07]; P=0.038; I2=75%). Incontrast, the meta-analysis of the case-control studies (9 effect sizes) showed a non-significant increase in risk (ES: 1.16; 95% CI:[0.71-1.88]; P=0.542; I2=82%). CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates that marijuana smoking may increase lung cancer risk, with cohort studies showing asignificant twofold association. Although case-control studies were not statistically significant, the upward trend highlights theimportance of considering cannabis use in lung cancer risk assessments and patient counseling.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. METHODS: To construct an Entosis-related Prognostic Prediction Index (EPPI), this study integrated TCGA-LUAD transcriptomic, clinical, and somatic mutation data. Three independent GEO cohorts provided external validation. The initial candidate gene set covered components driving cell-in-cell formation and the intracellular degradation of internalized cells. For subgroup comparison, the analytical approach incorporated survival analysis, functional enrichment, tumor microenvironment profiling, mutation analysis, immunotherapy assessment, and drug-sensitivity prediction. Tissue and cellular distributions of the EPPI genes were mapped using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing. Molecular docking assessed predicted drug-target interactions. Finally, in vitro RAC1 knockdown experiments evaluated the cellular function of a representative EPPI gene. RESULTS: Comprising RND3, RAC1, KRAS, CTNNA1, AURKA, and ACTB, the final EPPI consistently stratified overall survival across all cohorts and showed moderate prognostic discrimination. The high-EPPI group had greater tumor purity and mutational burden, with enhanced cell-cycle, DNA-repair, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and NF-κB programs, whereas the low-EPPI group showed greater immune and stromal infiltration. TIDE and immunophenoscores also differed between subgroups. Drug-response models predicted greater sensitivity to cisplatin and paclitaxel in the high-EPPI group and to several targeted agents in the low-EPPI group. Molecular docking predicted RAC1-EHT-1864 and AURKA-alisertib interactions. Spatial and single-cell analyses showed heterogeneous EPPI-gene expression, with ACTB and RAC1 broadly distributed and AURKA restricted to selected populations. RAC1 depletion suppressed LUAD-cell proliferation, DNA synthesis, migration, and invasion. CONCLUSION: The EPPI is an entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification in LUAD. Based on this index, patients can be separated into subgroups with distinct proliferative features, genomic alterations, tissue compositions, and predicted drug sensitivities. These findings associate entosis-related molecular features with distinct cellular and clinical characteristics of LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a critical clinical challenge in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with 40%-60% of progressing patients lacking an identifiable genetic resistance driver. Through quantitative secretomic profiling of paired osimertinib-sensitive and -resistant NSCLC cell lines, we identified laminin subunit γ2 (LAMC2) as markedly enriched in resistant cell secretomes. Single-cell RNA sequencing reanalysis revealed a LAMC2-high drug-tolerant persister subpopulation that expanded under osimertinib pressure, with pseudotime analysis suggesting progressive co-upregulation of LAMC2 and matrix metalloproteinase 14 (MMP14) along the treatment-to-resistance trajectory. Across four independent cohorts, MMP14 exhibited the strongest co-expression with LAMC2 among all metalloproteinases; the two proteins also physically interacted, and their concurrent high expression predicted the worst overall survival. Mechanistically, MMP14 cleaved LAMC2 to release a bioactive Domain III (DIII) fragment harboring EGF-like repeats, which reactivated EGFR/AKT/ERK signaling despite continued osimertinib exposure. Exogenous DIII conferred resistance in sensitive cells, whereas an anti-DIII blocking antibody reversed MMP14-driven resistance in cell lines and patient-derived organoids. The selective MMP14 inhibitor NSC405020 restored osimertinib sensitivity in vitro and suppressed xenograft growth. In residual tumor tissues from neoadjuvant osimertinib-treated patients, non-responders exhibited higher LAMC2/MMP14 co-expression and more prominent spatial exclusion of CD8⁺ T-cells from the tumor core compared with major pathological responders. These findings identify the MMP14-LAMC2-DIII proteolytic axis as a non-genetic resistance mechanism and suggest that MMP14 inhibition or DIII neutralization may represent a rational strategy to overcome acquired osimertinib resistance.

papers.abstract_en: PD-L1-mediated immunosuppression is a key mechanism underlying tumor immune evasion, whereas PD-1/PD-L1 blockade therapies remain limited by low response rates and acquired resistance. Through small-molecule screening, we identify isobavachalcone (IBC), a naturally derived compound that modulates PD-L1 homeostasis by targeting the deubiquitinase OTUB1. Mechanistically, IBC targets OTUB1 at the His217 residue and suppresses its deubiquitinase activity, thereby promoting K48-linked polyubiquitination of PD-L1 and its proteasome-dependent degradation. Functionally, IBC reduces tumor cell PD-L1 expression and enhances CD8+ T cell-mediated cytotoxicity. In PD-L1-deficient tumor models, IBC fails to further enhance antitumor activity, indicating that PD-L1 is required for IBC-mediated immune regulation. Moreover, IBC combined with anti-CTLA-4 therapy further enhanced antitumor efficacy. Together, these findings highlight IBC as a potential drug candidate that promotes PD-L1 degradation and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of targeting the OTUB1-PD-L1 axis to improve immune checkpoint therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Accumulating evidence has shown that the dysfunction of mitochondria, the multifunctional organelles in various cellular processes, is a pivotal event in the development of various diseases, including human cancers. The molecular alterations in tumors that promote metabolic diversity and distinct targetable dependencies remain poorly defined. The mitochondrial transporter SLC25A20, also known as carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase (CACT), is crucial for fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) by importing acylcarnitines into the mitochondrial matrix. Here, we demonstrate that SLC25A20 is significantly upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) tissues and cells, and its expression correlates with poor patient survival. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments reveal that SLC25A20 promotes tumor cell proliferation, survival, migration, and invasion by enhancing FAO-associated mitochondrial bioenergetics and suppressing apoptosis. Mechanistically, SLC25A20-mediated FAO maintains mitochondrial function and supports oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), thereby sustaining tumor bioenergetics and redox homeostasis. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing of SLC25A20 impairs tumor growth in vivo. These findings establish SLC25A20 as a key metabolic driver in LUAD and suggest it may be a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a common severe complication of advanced lung cancer and significantly worsens prognosis. Physical targeted therapies, represented by piezocatalytic therapy, sonodynamic therapy, photodynamic therapy, hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy, radiofrequency ablation and thermosensitive in situ hydrogel drug delivery system, induce reactive oxygen species generation via light, ultrasound, or piezocatalytic energy, or achieve tumor killing through local hyperthermia and temperature-controlled drug release, offering new strategies for MPE. However, existing reviews mostly focus on single modalities, lacking systematic classification and suitability comparison based on the pleural microenvironment and respiratory mechanics. This review summarizes their mechanisms, biological effects, and translational status in the context of pleural anatomy and pathological microenvironment, and highlights multi-field combination, microenvironment remodeling, and precise energy regulation as future directions for MPE therapy. .

papers.abstract_en: Medical Vision Foundation Models (MVFMs) mark a shift from task-specific artificial intelligence (AI) toward general-purpose visual intelligence in medical imaging. However, clinical deployment remains constrained by tensions among data availability, technological development, and integration into clinical workflows. To address these issues, this review provides a systematic analysis of the field's evolution from 2019 to 2025. We introduce the Data-Technology-Translation Triad as a unifying conceptual framework to structure the progress, key factors, and challenges of MVFMs. Our analysis traces the field's development and identifies a convergence toward Transformer-based and hybrid architectures, alongside hybrid pre-training paradigms. We present a unified technical framework that covers pre-training strategies, including generative, contrastive, and hybrid learning, as well as adaptation mechanisms such as full fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and prompt learning. Furthermore, we examine how data scarcity, heterogeneity, and privacy constraints in medical imaging drive the adoption of self-supervised learning and highlight domain generalization as a critical research direction. Although MVFMs demonstrate strong performance in data-efficient and multi-task settings, their clinical translation is hindered by limited generalization, insufficient interpretability, misalignment with clinical workflows, and regulatory uncertainty. In response, we propose practical directions for developing reliable general-purpose medical vision systems, with emphasis on causal reasoning, dynamic data learning, interactive human-AI collaboration, and coordinated efforts among researchers, clinicians, and regulators. This review provides a structured reference to guide MVFMs from technical validation to clinically effective, reliable, and ethically sound deployment. An updated collection of MVFM papers and related resources is available at our website https://github.com/ice-TuoShui/MVFM-Review.

papers.abstract_en: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) have advanced the study of complex lung diseases by resolving cellular heterogeneity, tissue architecture, and intercellular communication. These technologies are particularly informative in chronic respiratory disorders, where pathological remodeling involves coordinated alterations across epithelial, stromal, immune, and endothelial compartments. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a rare fatal fibrotic disorder, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a prevalent heterogeneous respiratory condition, represent distinct chronic lung diseases shaped by persistent injury, maladaptive repair, and progressive tissue remodeling. However, current understanding of their pathogenesis remains incomplete, and conventional approaches lack the resolution to define disease-associated cell states, spatially restricted niches, or compartment-specific interactions. This review synthesizes recent scRNA-seq and ST studies in IPF and COPD, emphasizing how high-resolution atlases refine established pathobiological frameworks and reveal shared and disease-specific cellular programs. We highlight epithelial dysfunction and impaired progenitor repair as shared mechanistic features of IPF and COPD, while emphasizing alveolar regenerative failure, fibroblast activation, and profibrotic niche formation as central features of IPF, and compartment-specific airway remodeling, inflammatory epithelial states, and emphysema-associated parenchymal injury as prominent features of COPD. We further discuss stromal and immune remodeling, hypoxia-associated vascular remodeling, and the translational implications of these findings for molecular stratification, target prioritization, and mechanism-informed therapeutic development, while noting limitations related to end-stage tissue sampling, platform constraints, and mouse-human correspondence. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding the cellular and spatial mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis and translational relevance of IPF and COPD.

papers.abstract_en: As one of the malignant tumors with high incidence and mortality worldwide, lung cancer features high heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance, which severely impair the prognosis of patients with lung cancer. In recent years, novel cell death modes such as ferroptosis, cuproptosis, disulfidptosis and necrosis by sodium overload have become research hotspots in oncology. Focusing on these four forms of cell death, this review systematically clarifies their roles in lung cancer initiation and progression, regulation of the tumor microenvironment, and therapeutic resistance; summarizes related prognostic biomarkers and representative prognostic models; and discusses the crosstalk among multiple cell death pathways and advances in clinical translation. This review aims to provide a reference for improving prognostic assessment in lung cancer, elucidating mechanisms of therapeutic resistance, and developing novel antitumor strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Biallelic pathogenic variants in UBR7, encoding ubiquitin protein ligase E3 component n-recognin 7, cause Li-Campeau syndrome (LICAS; OMIM #619189), which is characterized by developmental delay/intellectual disability, epilepsy, hypothyroidism, ptosis, genital anomalies, and cardiac anomalies. Here, we report an 18-year-old female patient with dysmorphic facial features, ptosis, congenital hypothyroidism, intellectual disability, stereotypic hand movements, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, hepatosplenomegaly, and toenail hypoplasia. In contrast to previously reported patients, all of whom presented with global developmental delay, our patient achieved age-appropriate early motor and language milestones, representing the mildest early developmental course reported in LICAS to date. Exome sequencing revealed a homozygous deletion encompassing Exon 7 of UBR7, representing the first single-exon deletion reported in this gene. This report expands both the phenotypic and genotypic spectrum of LICAS and underscores the clinical utility of Next generation sequencing-based copy-number variant analysis in the diagnostic workup of rare diseases.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Multi-cancer detection (MCD) tests currently being tested in clinical trials may be a scalable, convenient means to improve cancer screening, yet little is known about the potential clinical and psychosocial consequences of doing so in underserved communities. OBJECTIVE: To summarize the current literature examining potential clinical and psychosocial outcomes and consequences for MCD testing in underserved populations. METHODS: We searched and then reviewed articles from five databases: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane. For inclusion, studies had to primarily focus on MCD testing within underserved populations. Out of 376 articles identified, 29 met inclusion criteria. RESULTS: Financial constraints were the most frequently cited barrier (n = 23). 24 articles mentioned clinical consequences and nine mentioned psychosocial consequences, with the most common being lower rates of cancer screening with proven existing recommended tests (n = 10) and emotional stress, worry, and anxiety (n = 11), respectively. Many expressed concerns about underrepresentation in clinical trials. CONCLUSIONS: The review highlights common potential clinical consequences as well as important factors underserved populations may face if/when MCD testing is implemented in their healthcare. Future prospective studies, experimental and observational, should intentionally include underrepresented patient populations to better understand and address these challenges.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Lung transplantation (LT) improves survival in patients with end-stage lung disease; however, recovery of physical function after transplantation remains insufficiently characterized, particularly in critically ill recipients bridged with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Understanding longitudinal functional recovery and potential differences between ECMO and non-ECMO recipients is essential for optimizing post-transplant rehabilitation strategies. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 84 adult patients who underwent lung or heart-lung transplantation between 2018 and 2023. Physical function was assessed at 6 and 12 months using the 6-minute walk test, gait speed, and strength measures. Changes over time and group differences were evaluated using longitudinal statistical models. RESULTS: Fifty patients (59.5%) required ECMO support. Overall physical function significantly improved from 6 to 12 months, with 93.4% achieving independent ambulation by 12 months. ECMO recipients had a lower proportion of independent ambulation at 6 months compared with non-ECMO recipients. At 12 months, no statistically significant between-group difference was observed in the proportion of patients achieving independent ambulation. CONCLUSIONS: LT recipients showed significant improvement in physical function between 6 and 12 months after transplantation. ECMO-bridged recipients had lower independent ambulation rates at 6 months, while no statistically significant between-group difference was observed at 12 months. Further studies incorporating pretransplant and early postoperative assessments are needed to better characterize functional recovery after lung transplantation.

papers.abstract_en: Radiation dose to the heart is associated with various cardiac side effects. However, the specific cardiac and pulmonary structures that contribute to these toxicities remain incompletely understood. Moreover, although multiple factors contribute to reduced survival after radiotherapy, the role of radiation-induced cardiac toxicity remains underrecognized. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the associations between radiation dose to specific cardiac and pulmonary structures, cardiac side effects, and survival. A total of 137 clinical studies were analysed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Associations between radiation dose and cardiac side effects were identified not only for the whole heart but also for specific cardiac substructures, including myocardial segments, coronary arteries, and the pericardium. Notably, radiation dose to the lungs was also associated with decline in cardiac function, suggesting that minimizing cardiac toxicity may require consideration of both local cardiac irradiation and non-local irradiation of adjacent organs, particularly the lungs. Direct evidence linking cardiac side effects to survival was limited. Nevertheless, the observed associations between higher radiation doses, increased cardiac toxicity, and poorer survival suggest a potential relationship that warrants further investigation. These findings support the hypothesis that reducing specific cardiac side effects may benefit from targeted sparing of the relevant cardiac and pulmonary substructures. While many radiation-related cardiac side effects are now recognized, further research is needed to identify and characterize previously unrecognized manifestations and to clarify their contribution to long-term survival.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Variants in YWHAG cause severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) with early-onset seizures. METHODS: In this study, 55 YWHAG missense variants were curated, including 17 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants that met ACMG guideline criteria and 38 benign variants from gnomAD. We also evaluated 34 pathogenicity prediction tools using accuracy, balanced accuracy, AUC, and MCC. RESULTS: Protein structure modeling revealed that hydrogen bond alterations occurred in both pathogenic and benign YWHAG variants, which could not reliably distinguish the two groups. YWHAG was highly expressed in the central nervous system with three distinct developmental peaks, shifting from both excitatory and inhibitory neurons to predominantly excitatory neurons during cerebral organoid maturation. The YWHAG protein regulated the MAPK, PI3K-Akt, Hippo pathways and cell cycle progression. Among the 34 evaluated tools, deep learning and ensemble algorithms outperformed traditional conservation-based predictors, with MetaSVM showing the best overall performance, MetaLR achieving excellent specificity and ESM1b attaining the highest AUC value. CONCLUSION: Meta-predictors may effectively predict YWHAG missense variant pathogenicity, and YWHAG spatiotemporal expression aligns with its DEE pathogenic role. These computational tools may provide reliable support for the pathogenicity assessment of YWHAG variants in clinical genetic diagnosis.
