papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous disease with distinct inflammatory profiles that may be associated with key pathological features, including emphysema and airway wall remodeling. This study aimed to identify COPD subgroups based on circulating pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine activity and airflow limitation and to examine their clinical, physiological, and quantitative CT characteristics. METHODS: Demographic characteristics, symptom scores, pulmonary function parameters, and quantitative CT indices were collected from patients with stable COPD. Serum levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Cluster analysis was performed using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). RESULTS: A total of 319 stable COPD patients were included. Four distinct clusters were identified. Cluster 1 (Severe-low inflammation) was characterized by the lowest circulating inflammatory cytokine levels, the greatest symptom burden, the most severe airflow limitation, an increased exacerbation frequency, and the most extensive emphysema. Cluster 2 (Mild-low inflammation) exhibited low levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, mild symptoms, relatively preserved lung function, and a low frequency of annual exacerbations. Cluster 3 (Moderate-elevated inflammation) had moderately elevated levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, with intermediate mMRC and CAT scores, pulmonary function impairment and exacerbation frequency. Cluster 4 (Extremely high inflammation) was characterized by markedly elevated levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, intermediate symptom burden, relatively preserved pulmonary function, pronounced airway wall thickening and a high frequency of moderate-to-severe exacerbations. Further cytokine ratio analysis revealed an IL-6-related shift in Clusters 3 and 4 and an IL-17-related shift predominantly in Cluster 3. CONCLUSION: Integrating cytokine profiles with airflow limitation identified four exploratory COPD phenotypes, highlighting a potential dissociation between systemic inflammation and disease severity. External and longitudinal validation is needed to confirm their reproducibility and clinical relevance.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Pulmonary fungal infections are increasingly recognized as important complications of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but early identification remains challenging. This study investigated the independent association between peak expiratory flow (PEF) and pulmonary fungal infection in hospitalized patients with AECOPD. METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 729 adult inpatients with AECOPD admitted to a tertiary hospital in Chongqing from January to December 2023. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between PEF and pulmonary fungal infection. Subgroup and mediation analyses were also performed. RESULTS: The mean age was 71.7 years, and 68.4% were male. Patients with pulmonary fungal infection were older and had lower PEF values than those without infection (2.1 ± 0.9 vs 2.4 ± 1.3, respectively), and showed higher ESR, CRP, and IL-6 levels. After covariate adjustment, higher PEF was independently associated with a lower risk of pulmonary fungal infection (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.98, P = 0.034). This association remained consistent across age, sex, and smoking subgroups, without significant interactions. Age partially mediated this association, accounting for 15.68% of the total effect. CONCLUSION: Lower PEF was independently associated with increased pulmonary fungal infection risk in hospitalized patients with AECOPD. PEF may serve as a simple bedside indicator for early risk stratification and targeted clinical evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are at an elevated risk of fungal infections, yet reliable tools for early risk stratification are lacking. This study aimed to analyze the risk factors associated with fungal infections in patients with COPD and to develop a predictive model. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed patients with COPD who were admitted to Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital, between June 2021 and June 2023. Demographic and clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. The risk factors were explored by univariate logistic regression and stepwise multivariate logistic regressions. Model performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic curve and area under the curve (AUC), along with calibration and decision curve analyses. The internal validation was performed using Bootstrap (n=1000) method. RESULTS: A total of 498 patients with COPD were enrolled, with 78 patients in the fungal infection group. Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that PaO2 within the normal range (OR=2.04, 95% CI: 1.12-3.71, P=0.02) and mold mix specific IgE above the normal threshold (OR=2.37, 95% CI: 1.04-5.36, P=0.04) were independently associated with an increased risk of fungal infections, whereas lymphocyte counts within the normal range (OR=0.37, 95% CI: 0.21-0.63, P<0.01) were associated with a reduced risk. Procalcitonin, albumin, and medical history of COPD duration were also included in predictive model based on the regression analysis. The AUC was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.68-0.79), and the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test and decision curves indicated good differentiation and calibration. CONCLUSION: This study identifies elevated PaO2, mold mix specific IgE and lymphocyte counts as risk factors for fungal infections. The predictive model incorporating PaO2, mold mix specific IgE, lymphocyte counts, procalcitonin, albumin, and medical history of COPD duration demonstrated good predictive performance, offering a potential tool for early identification of high-risk patients in clinical practice.

papers.abstract_en: The purpose of this study is to determine the smallest tested fraction of manually labeled training data required for a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) classifier to achieve satisfactory MRI series classification performance (macro-F1 ≥ 0.80) across five heterogeneous public MRI datasets using digital imaging and communications in medicine (DICOM) metadata, image data, or both. This retrospective study included 3804 examinations and 14,054 MRI series from five public DICOM datasets spanning brain, knee, lumbar spine, liver, and breast MRI, accessed February-April 2026. AI classification models included a random forest classifier using DICOM header metadata, a deep convolutional neural network classifier using the geometric center slice of each MRI series, and decision-fusion models. Models were trained with 5%-40% of studies manually labeled in 5-percentage-point increments, with additional 1%-4% fractions for the knee and lumbar spine. Model performance was evaluated on the remaining studies using study-level splits across five random seeds. Results were summarized as mean ± standard deviation. Zero-label unsupervised clustering results were evaluated separately on the full dataset. The macro-F1 target was reached at the smallest tested training fraction of 1% in the lumbar spine (0.945 ± 0.013), at 2% in the knee (0.818 ± 0.006), at 10% in the brain (0.872 ± 0.027), and at 20% in the liver (0.827 ± 0.016) and the breast (0.847 ± 0.012). The best-performing model differed by dataset, reflecting different contributions from metadata versus image data. Across five separately evaluated public MRI datasets, at least one header-based, image-based, or combined model achieved macro-F1 ≥ 0.80 using no more than 20% manually labeled studies.

papers.abstract_en: Mandibular odontogenic cysts can complicate surgical planning if located near the mandibular canal. Accurate delineation of both structures is therefore clinically important. This study presents a deep learning-based method for simultaneously segmenting mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. The developed method relies on a hybrid deep learning architecture integrating a ConvNeXt-Base encoder, a Dilated Context Block, a U-Net-based decoder, and a Deep Supervision mechanism. This framework simultaneously segments the mandibular canal and odontogenic cyst regions within the same architecture, promoting multi-scale contextual feature learning. We evaluated the performance of the proposed method using fivefold cross-validation experiments on a real-world clinical CBCT dataset comprising 103 patient images. We assessed segmentation performance using overlap-based metrics together with boundary-aware HD95 and ASSD metrics. The experimental results demonstrated that the model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 76.28% ± 1.83%. Excluding the background class yielded macro IoU and macro F1-score values of 64.46% ± 2.74% and 77.00% ± 1.89%, respectively. Meanwhile, the weighted IoU and weighted F1-score values were 78.71% ± 4.25% and 87.63% ± 2.63%, respectively. In boundary-based evaluations, the mandibular canal had an HD95 of 2.44 ± 2.98 mm and an ASSD of 0.45 ± 0.30 mm. The corresponding values for odontogenic cysts were 5.59 ± 3.65 mm and 1.43 ± 0.88 mm, respectively. These results suggest that the mandibular canal is more consistently delineated, while cyst segmentation remains more challenging, particularly at irregular and low-contrast boundaries. The proposed framework allows for the simultaneous and objective segmentation of mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal within a unified, multi-class CBCT analysis framework. By providing reproducible delineation of both structures, this method could serve as a technical foundation for future quantitative analyses of lesion-canal relationships. However, further validation using larger, multicenter, volumetric CBCT datasets is required before clinical translation.

papers.abstract_en: The radiology report is essential for directing the course of treatment for a patient. However, writing radiology reports is a huge burden for radiologists. Manual reporting faces challenges due to intra-labeler and inter-labeler variability, causing inconsistent patient treatment and diagnostic results, and complicating matters due to alertness and changing judgment. To address these challenges, we propose an automated radiology report generation model tailored for chest X-ray imaging. We introduce BLIX-Ray, a vision-language model (VLM) designed to generate radiology reports using a transfer learning approach. BLIX-Ray fine-tunes the pre-trained BLIP model to extract and align rich visual and textual representations suited to the medical imaging domain. We use reinforcement learning (RL) to directly optimize report generation based on language evaluation metrics in order to further enhance performance. We evaluate BLIX-Ray on two publicly available datasets: IU-Xray and CheXpert Plus. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves the highest CIDEr and BERTScore on both datasets, while n-gram-oriented baselines retain an advantage on BLEU. BLIX-Ray integrates reinforcement learning and transfer learning to improve medical report generation under limited and heterogeneous data conditions. The results highlight the potential of vision-language models to support automated and standardized radiology reporting. Notably, BLIX-Ray achieves the best reported CIDEr (0.6534) and BERTScore (0.8765) among the compared methods on IU-Xray and leads on CIDEr, METEOR, and BERTScore on CheXpert Plus (BERTScore 0.8407), demonstrating strong report-level consensus and semantic similarity with the reference reports.

papers.abstract_en: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is the most common cause of vestibular vertigo, yet accurate diagnosis remains challenging without specialist expertise. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic algorithm for BPPV using video-nystagmography (VNG) recordings. A total of 1352 VNG recordings were collected from patients with posterior semicircular canal (PSCC) BPPV (n = 234), lateral semicircular canal (LSCC) BPPV (canalolithiasis, n = 188; cupulolithiasis, n = 58), and healthy controls (n = 224) at a single tertiary referral hospital, yielding 1738 signal segments (1312 nystagmus segments annotated by two otolaryngologists and 426 normal segments). Eye trajectory signals were extracted using a deep learning-based VNG eye-tracking algorithm, transformed into two-dimensional (2D) scalogram representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT), and classified using task-specific backbone architectures selected through systematic comparison under a patient-level data split. Ablation analysis showed that CWT-based 2D representations significantly outperformed raw one-dimensional (1D) time-series baselines. The final models achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values of 0.974 for horizontal and 0.961 for torsional nystagmus classification. For BPPV subtype diagnosis, recording-level accuracy was 0.935 for the PSCC and 0.938 for the LSCC evaluation; F1-scores exceeded 0.84 for all PSCC classes and ranged from 0.59 to 0.98 for LSCC classes, with canalolithiasis variants outperforming cupulolithiasis variants. These findings suggest the feasibility of AI-assisted BPPV diagnosis from VNG recordings.

papers.abstract_en: Major histocompatibility complex class Ia (MHC-Ia)-restricted CD8⁺ T cell responses play a central role in the host defense against HIV-1, with certain MHC-Ia alleles known to be associated with cytotoxic T lymphocyte responses having an increased potential for viral control. However, the impact of immune aging on the effectiveness of such protective alleles remains unclear. In this study, we assessed SIVmac239 replication in aged (17-23 yr old) rhesus macaques (RMs) exhibiting low frequencies of naïve T cells and expanded effector memory T cells, that were further stratified by the presence (MHC⁺) or absence (MHC-) of 3 known "protective MHC-Ia alleles" (Mamu-A*01, Mamu-B*08, or Mamu-B*17). All RMs were infected with SIVmac239 and viral dynamics monitored longitudinally. MHC⁺ RMs demonstrated significantly lower plasma viral loads (PVLs) through 70 d postinfection compared with MHC- RMs. At 70 d postinfection, half of the RMs from each group initiated suppressive triple antiretroviral therapy comprising dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) for 15 wk, followed by suboptimal TDF monotherapy for an additional 21 wk. While antiretroviral therapy substantially reduced PVL in both groups, viral decline was accelerated in MHC⁺ RMs relative to MHC- RMs. Moreover, upon switching to TDF monotherapy, PVL rebounded by almost 3 logs in MHC- RMs, while MHC⁺ RMs maintained viral suppression. Collectively, these findings indicate that protective MHC-Ia alleles can mediate viral control in aged hosts, even under suboptimal treatment conditions, and highlight the potential role of optimized CD8+ T cell responses in strategies targeting viral persistence in aging populations.

papers.abstract_en: Robotic surgical platforms are diversifying, and clinical outcomes are increasingly comparable across systems, yet the console surgeon's subjective experience remains poorly characterized. We developed a surgeon-reported questionnaire on robotic surgical systems and performed a preliminary psychometric evaluation in robotic radical prostatectomy. The Surgeons' Perception Questionnaire on Robotics (SPQR) includes 31 five-point items in six domains: technical and operational aspects, key surgical tasks, ergonomics and physical comfort, communication and workflow integration, learning curve, and overall evaluation. In a cross-sectional web-based survey, surgeons rated the platform they primarily used for robotic radical prostatectomy. Internal consistency was assessed with polychoric-based Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega; exploratory (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) were performed in the same sample. Fifty-nine surgeons participated (response rate 42%); 81% evaluated the da Vinci Xi. Overall internal consistency was high (alpha 0.96; omega 0.97). Alpha and omega were ≥ 0.84 in five domains but below 0.70 for ergonomics and physical comfort (0.64 and 0.67). EFA suggested three factors (system performance and satisfaction; learning curve and training; ergonomics). CFA showed high incremental fit (comparative fit index 0.985) but inadequate absolute fit (root mean square error of approximation 0.097; standardized root mean square residual 0.135), and the ergonomics factor was weakly defined. The SPQR showed high internal consistency in most domains and a provisional multidimensional structure. Because the sample was small, highly experienced, predominantly male, and dominated by one platform, these findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts before the SPQR is used for platform comparisons.

papers.abstract_en: Robot-assisted surgery has spread from urology into several other surgical fields, and different categories of robotic system are now coded separately in Germany. This nationwide descriptive time-series analysis used aggregated hospital data of the Institute for the Hospital Remuneration System for 2019 to 2025. All inpatient hospital cases carrying at least one code of the group for use of a surgical robot (group 5-987 of the German Operation and Procedure Classification) were included, and annual case volume, the coded robot categories, principal diagnoses grouped at the three-character level, sex, age, clinical complexity and length of stay were described, together with selected index procedures counted with and without a robot code. The annual number of cases increased 3.78-fold, from 32,691 in 2019 to 123,706 in 2025, and rose in every year. Prostate cancer remained the most frequent principal diagnosis group: its case number almost doubled from 14,796 to 29,407 while its share fell from 45.3% to 23.8%. Osteoarthritis of knee became the second most frequent, rising from 1,936 to 21,447 cases. The proportion of female cases increased from 26.1% to 40.9%. Among hospital cases with the code for radical prostatovesiculectomy, the proportion also carrying a robot code rose from 52.9% to 85.1%, and for knee endoprosthesis implantation from 1.1% to 8.9%. Recorded robot-associated inpatient hospital activity almost quadrupled over seven years, and both the coded robot categories and the diagnostic composition broadened. These data describe recorded activity and its composition but do not provide information on outcomes, costs or appropriateness.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sagittal spinal parameters are used to assess upright alignment during growth. OBJECTIVE: To describe sagittal spinopelvic parameters and assess their associations with age and sex in children and adolescents in Turkey. RESULTS: Mean (standard deviation) pelvic incidence, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, lumbar lordosis, and thoracic kyphosis were 45.4 (12.3)°, 11.3 (6.9)°, 34.2 (10.4)°, 57.5 (13.8)°, and 46.0 (13.4)°, respectively; sagittal vertical axis was 46.6 (27.6) mm. C2, T4, and L1 tilts were 5.0 (2.9)°, 10.4 (4.6)°, and 9.0 (4.7)°; T4 pelvic angle and L1 pelvic angle were 4.1 (3.1)° and 3.4 (3.1)°. Lumbar lordosis showed the largest adjusted age coefficient (1.81°/year; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.28-2.34; adjusted R2=0.121). T4 pelvic angle and L1 pelvic angle did not differ significantly across age groups (P=0.308 and P=0.966). CONCLUSION: In children and adolescents without radiographic spinal or pelvic deformity, lumbar lordosis had the clearest cross-sectional association with age. No statistically significant age-group differences were detected for T4 pelvic angle or L1 pelvic angle. These data provide clinically relevant standing-radiograph reference data for sagittal spinopelvic parameters.

A greater number of cholangitis episodes was associated with a higher likelihood of LT (odds ratio: 1.08, 95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.16, p = 0.044). Corticosteroids were prescribed to 96% of patients, and a longer treatment duration was associated with higher complication rates. About 1.8% of patients developed acute kidney injury, with no progression to end-stage renal disease. CONCLUSION: Postoperative cholangitis remains an important clinical factor associated with LT in infants with BA. Corticosteroid treatment duration may reflect underlying disease severity rather than therapeutic benefit. Renal complications are uncommon. Optimizing postoperative care-particularly timely cholangitis management-is essential to improve outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 250 ELBWIs (< 1000 g) treated from 2013 to 2022; 22 developed S-NEC. Eleven coagulation and fibrinolysis markers were measured within 24 h of birth. S-NEC incidence increased across risk categories (3.7%, 14.5%, and 19.6%; p for trend = 0.013). CONCLUSIONS: Hemostatic abnormalities at birth were associated with subsequent S-NEC in ELBWIs, suggesting perinatal or intrauterine origins. The risk score showed a high NPV and may serve as a practical rule-out tool for early neonatal intensive care unit stratification.

CONCLUSION: The postoperative administration of ASX induced beneficial effects, resulting in the reduction of hepatic fibrosis via mechanisms involving the inhibition of NF-κB expression and improvement of AQP8 expression and enhancement of compensatory MRP3 activity.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing chemotherapy. The rising incidence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) further challenges the adequacy of empirical antimicrobial therapy. Therefore, this study aimed to identify features associated with different microbiological profiles of BSIs in chemotherapy patients using machine learning models. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1435 confirmed BSI episodes among 1220 patients treated at a tertiary cancer center from 2017 to 2022. A multi-label classification approach was used to model BSIs associated with carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CR-GNB), methicillin-resistant staphylococci, third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (3GCRE), fungal pathogens, and non-MDRO/non-fungal. Classifier chain models based on logistic regression, random forests, neural networks, and gradient boosting were trained and evaluated using cross-validation with an independent test set. Model outputs were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to estimate feature contributions. RESULTS: Most BSIs occurred during the first chemotherapy cycle and were due to non-MDROs or fungal agents (1193 episodes; 83.1%), CR-GNB was identified in 109 (7.6%). Model performance varied across pathogen groups, with the highest discrimination observed for CR-GNB (AUC-ROC 83.25%; 95% CI 73.91%-91.64%). Key features included hospitalization days, hematologic malignancy, prior MDRO infection, monocytopenia, and palliative chemotherapy. Chemotherapy class contributed differently across pathogen groups, with alkylating agents contributing to candidemia, antitumor antibiotics to CR-GNB, and antimetabolites to 3GCRE. Prior CR-GNB infection was the strongest predictor for CR-GNB BSI, while palliative chemotherapy correlated with non-MDRO/non-fungal BSI. CONCLUSION: Multi-label machine learning approaches may help disentangle the complex etiologies of BSIs in cancer patients by identifying associations between host factors, prior MDRO infection, and chemotherapy class within confirmed BSI episodes, informing future hypothesis generation.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundPleural aspiration has limited diagnostic yield in malignant (MPE) and tuberculous pleural effusions (TPE), more so when requiring molecular profiling in MPE and due to the paucibacillary nature of TPE. In our institution, patients with suspected MPE or TPE are offered a straight-to-biopsy approach with pleural biopsy as the initial diagnostic procedure, or a pleural aspiration-first approach, through shared decision-making.ObjectivesTo compare clinical outcomes between a straight-to-biopsy strategy and a pleural aspiration-first approach in patients diagnosed with MPE or TPE.DesignWe performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent pleural procedures for unilateral effusions between January 2022 and February 2025 and were diagnosed with MPE or TPE. We excluded patients with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group status ≥ 3 and patients with a pre-existing, established diagnosis of metastatic cancer who had pleural procedures performed for non-diagnostic intent.MethodsClinical outcomes were compared between a straight-to-biopsy versus pleural aspiration-first approach.Results271 patients were included (mean age 67 years, SD 15); 74.9% had MPE and 25.1% had TPE. Straight-to-biopsy and pleural aspiration-first approaches were undertaken in 44.3% and 55.7% of patients, respectively. Most patients in the straight-to-biopsy group underwent medical thoracoscopy (92.5%, 111/120), with concurrent talc pleurodesis performed in 55 patients. Compared with pleural aspiration-first, a straight-to-biopsy approach was associated with a shorter time to actionable diagnosis (16 (IQR:9-21) vs 23 (IQR:16-40) days; p<0.001), earlier treatment initiation (22 (IQR:16-33) vs 27 (IQR:18-43) days; p=0.023), shorter hospitalisation for diagnostic evaluation (4 (IQR:3-5) vs 8 (IQR:5-13) days; p<0.001), and were less likely to require ≥2 diagnostic (3.3% vs 42.4%; p<0.001) or therapeutic pleural procedures (21.1% vs 50.0%; p<0.001).ConclusionIn patients with MPE or TPE, a straight-to-biopsy approach was associated with earlier diagnosis and treatment initiation, fewer repeat procedures, and shorter hospitalisation. Prospective studies are needed to establish its safety, clinical utility, and cost-effectiveness.

papers.abstract_en: Chromosome 3q (3q) amplification is a frequent event in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other cancer types, yet therapeutic strategies targeting oncogenic drivers within this amplicon have been unsuccessful. Our study revealed that the 3q amplicon encodes multiple Golgi-related proteins, including Phospholipase D1 (PLD1), which catalyzes the production of a potential oncogenic lipid, phosphatidic acid. We found that PLD1 is highly expressed in 3q-amplified NSCLC (3q-NSCLC) and its enzymatic activity is further boosted by coamplified PLD1 activator, ARF-like GTPase 14. High PLD1 activity is essential for 3q-NSCLC growth and metastasis. Mechanistically, PLD1 drives secretion of oncogenic factors via the carriers from the trans Golgi network to the cell surface pathway to support tumor growth. Transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC), which encodes a membrane protein, is coamplified with PLD1 and overexpressed in 3q-NSCLC. A TFRC antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) carrying a PLD1 inhibitor exhibited potential antitumor activity in mouse models. These findings establish PLD1 as a promoter of 3q-NSCLC and provide proof of concept for the development of PLD1-targeted therapies, including ADC-based approaches, for this challenging cancer subtype.

papers.abstract_en: Gastric intramural metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is rare, and chemotherapy-associated perforation is exceptionally uncommon. We report a case of a 67-year-old man with distal ESCC and a separate cardia squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). He declined esophagectomy and received definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) with paclitaxel, carboplatin, and 50.4 Gy radiotherapy. During the second chemotherapy cycle, the cardia tumor perforated and was treated by emergency omental patch repair. Chemoradiotherapy was subsequently completed. Three months after completion of dCRT, the esophageal lesion showed a clinical complete response, whereas residual cardia disease persisted. Extended total gastrectomy with splenectomy achieved R0 resection; pathology showed a 6-cm pT3 moderately differentiated SCC with partial treatment response and 0/12 positive nodes. Postoperative nivolumab was administered. This case illustrates a staged salvage strategy for persistent gastric intramural disease after definitive chemoradiotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lymphomas involving serous effusions as the initial clinical presentation are uncommon and pose significant diagnostic challenges because of their overlapping cytomorphologic features with reactive lymphocyte-rich effusions. Early diagnosis is crucial, particularly when tissue biopsy is difficult or inconclusive. AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the cytomorphologic spectrum of previously undiagnosed lymphoproliferative disorders presenting in serous effusions and to assess the complementary role of immunocytochemistry (ICC) and flow cytometry (FCM) in their diagnosis and subtyping. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive study was conducted at a tertiary cancer center over 10 years (January 2015-December 2024). Eighteen cases with an upfront diagnosis of lymphoma on pleural or ascitic fluid cytology were included. Cytomorphologic evaluation was performed on May-Grünwald-Giemsa and Papanicolaou-stained smears. Cell block-based ICC and multiparametric FCM were performed whenever indicated. Final diagnoses were established by integrating cytomorphology, immunophenotypic findings, and clinical correlation according to the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours. RESULTS: Among 12,092 serous effusion samples processed, 18 cases (0.15%) represented previously undiagnosed lymphomas diagnosed primarily on effusion cytology. The median age was 16 years (range: 8-55 years), with a male predominance (13 males and 5 females). Pleural effusions accounted for 83.3% of cases, and mediastinal mass was the most common presentation (83.3%). T-lymphoblastic lymphoma was the predominant subtype (12/18, 66.7%), followed by diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (3/18, 16.7%), high-grade B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable (2/18, 11.1%), and Burkitt lymphoma (1/18, 5.6%). ICC was particularly useful for diagnosing B-cell lymphomas, whereas FCM played a complementary role in T-lymphoblastic lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma. Five mediastinal biopsies were nondiagnostic because of hemorrhagic specimens, highlighting the diagnostic value of effusion cytology when tissue sampling was inadequate or not feasible. CONCLUSION: Serous effusion cytology, combined with ICC and FCM, is a valuable minimally invasive approach for the early diagnosis and subtyping of lymphomas presenting without prior tissue diagnosis. An integrated interpretation of cytomorphology, immunophenotyping, and clinical findings can facilitate timely diagnosis and appropriate clinical management, particularly in patients in whom tissue biopsy is difficult, delayed, or nondiagnostic.

papers.abstract_en: A series of twelve novel dihydropyrimidine (DHPM)-amide hybrid conjugates (6a-c, 8a-c, 10a-c, and 12a-c) were rationally designed, synthesized, and biologically evaluated as potential EGFR-targeted anticancer agents against A549 non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) cells. The target compounds were constructed via a convergent two-step protocol: Biginelli multicomponent condensation to assemble the DHPM-carboxylic acid core (4a-c), followed by EDC·HCl/HOBt-mediated chemoselective amide coupling with four clinically inspired amine fragments derived from erlotinib/gefitinib (series 10), cabozantinib (series 8), imatinib (series 12), and a sorafenib bioisostere (series 6). All compounds were characterized by IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and low-resolution ESI-MS. MTT cytotoxicity screening identified compound 10b as the most potent analogue (IC50 = 16.11 ± 0.11 µg mL-1, equivalent to 23.31 µM), exceeding the molar potency of the reference methotrexate (IC50 = 15.00 ± 0.48 µg mL-1, equivalent to 33.01 µM). It should be noted that methotrexate is a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor included solely as a general cytotoxicity control and is not a mechanistically matched EGFR comparator; the comparison therefore reflects relative cytotoxic potency only and does not imply EGFR selectivity. Molecular docking against EGFR (PDB 1M17), an erlotinib-bound inactive-conformation structure, returned the most favourable score for 10b (score = -7.819 kcal mol-1), with predicted hydrogen bonds to ASP831 and LYS721, a halogen contact at ILE765, and an extensive 15-residue hydrophobic network; these poses indicate compatibility with the erlotinib-binding pocket rather than a confirmed ATP-competitive binding mode. DFT calculations at B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) characterised the electronic structure of the isolated molecule (ΔE = 4.045 eV; ω = 3.155 eV) and are reported as a physicochemical description only, without implying a causal link to cellular activity. Normal mode analysis indicated conformational stability of the 10b-EGFR complex, collectively identifying 10b as a promising lead for further optimisation and mechanistic evaluation, for which direct EGFR kinase assays remain necessary.

papers.abstract_en: Thoracic surgery-related malpractice claims recorded in Catalonia (Spain) were collected from the Council of Medical Associations of Catalonia (CCMC, 1986-2024) and the Catalan Health Service (CatSalut, 2017-2024) databases. Of a total of 15,696 claims, 56 (0.4%) corresponded to the field of thoracic surgery. Lung cancer (51.8%) and pneumothorax (8.9%) were the most common diagnoses. Death occurred in 18 patients (31.2%). In relation to the reasons of allegations, in one patient with lung cancer undergoing lobectomy who died in the postoperative period, this information was missing. In the remaining 55 patients, causes of allegations included incorrect treatment in 31 (56.4%), diagnostic error in 11 (20%), unexpected complication in 8 (14.5%), infection in 4 (7.3%), and insufficient follow-up in 1 (1.8%). Of the 43 claims with a closed status, malpractice was established in 11 cases, with compensation ranging from €2000 to €154,581.44. Malpractice claims in thoracic surgery predominantly involved elective oncological procedures.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking has been linked to alterations in plasma protein profiles and increased risk of esophageal cancer (EC). However, the precise mediating roles of plasma proteins in this relationship remain unclear. This study explores the mediation effects of plasma proteins in smoking-associated EC, utilizing genetic proxies to uncover potential biological mechanisms underpinning this association. METHODS: Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were applied to examine the association between smoking traits and EC. Pathway enrichment analysis explored circulatory protein changes in smokers. A two-step mediation MR analysis identified key plasma proteins involved in smoking-related EC pathogenesis. Survival analysis assessed the impact of transcriptional levels of mediators on EC prognosis, while phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS) evaluated the safety of targeted molecules and investigated potential pleiotropy. The expression and function of ADH7 were evaluated by qRT-PCR and in vitro experiments. RESULTS: Genetic correlation analysis showed significant links between smoking and EC, supported by MR findings that confirmed a causal relationship. Smoking was found to influence pathways related to cytokine signaling, immune activation, and the STAT pathway. Five plasma proteins (ADH7, CPXM1, FUT3, GZMM, LYPD3) were identified as mediators in smoking-driven EC risk. Among these, ADH7 emerged as a key protein and was consistently associated with smoking traits; high ADH7 mRNA expression in EC tumor tissue was associated with reduced progression-free survival. PheWAS inferred that ADH7-targeted interventions might pose risks of neurological or psychiatric side effects, though these were not statistically significant. qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry showed that ADH7 was downregulated in EC tissues relative to adjacent normal mucosa, and functional assays demonstrated that overexpression of ADH7 suppressed the proliferative and migratory capacity of EC cells. Serum ELISA further revealed that circulating ADH7 concentrations were elevated in smokers and in EC patients, with the highest levels observed in smoking EC patients, supporting a role for smoking-driven elevation of circulating ADH7 in EC risk. CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals a compartment-specific, dual role for ADH7 in smoking-related EC: elevated circulating ADH7, driven in part by smoking, is associated with increased EC risk, whereas ADH7 acts as a tumor suppressor within esophageal tumor tissue. These findings provide novel genetic and mechanistic insights into smoking-related EC pathogenesis and highlight the importance of distinguishing circulating from tissue-level protein function when interpreting biomarker-disease associations.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To determine preliminary quantitative ADC thresholds for functional response and to evaluate whether integrating DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 provides complementary information for early systemic therapy response assessment in bone metastases. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included lung cancer patients with pelvic bone metastases who underwent three MRIs between November 2015 and November 2023: baseline, early time point (<4 months, TP1), and late (6-15 months, TP2) time points. ROC analysis based on lesion size change at TP2 determined ADC thresholds defining DWI response. A DWI response was defined as ADC >1300 µm²/s or ΔADC >0.14. An integrated response scheme (DWI-RECIST) combined this DWI-based response with RECIST assessment. Early responses at TP1 were compared between RECIST and DWI-RECIST using RECIST at TP2 as reference standard. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using net reclassification improvement and AUCs. RESULTS: Seventy-eight lesions from 27 patients were included. Compared with RECIST, DWI-RECIST yielded net classification gains of 7.4% (reader 1) and 11.1% (reader 2). DWI-RECIST showed higher AUCs than RECIST (reader 1: 0.6964 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.472; reader 2: 0.6415 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.781). Interobserver agreement for ADC was good (ICC 0.83-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ADC-derived DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 may provide complementary information for early assessment of pelvic bone metastases from lung cancer, particularly in lesions categorised as stable disease. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This pilot study proposes quantitative ADC thresholds and introduces a framework integrating these with RECIST 1.1 to support more objective response assessment in lung cancer pelvic bone metastases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Euphorbia species contain diverse secondary metabolites with reported biological activities, but Euphorbia petrophila remains pharmacologically underexplored. This study aimed to characterize the phytochemical profile of E. petrophila ethanol extract and evaluate its preliminary in vitro anticancer-related activity in lung and breast cancer cell models. METHODS: Aerial parts of E. petrophila were extracted with ethanol using ultrasonic-assisted extraction. The extract was profiled by LC-MS/MS. Cytotoxicity was assessed by MTT assay in A549 and MDA-MB-231 cancer cells and in BEAS-2B and MCF10A non-tumorigenic epithelial cells. Apoptosis and cell-cycle distribution were analyzed by flow cytometry. Migration and invasion were evaluated using Transwell assays, and selected gene-expression changes were measured by RT-qPCR. Data were analyzed using appropriate analysis of variance and post hoc comparisons. RESULTS: LC-MS/MS analysis identified phenolic acids and flavonoids, with gallic acid, quinic acid, ellagic acid, and isoquercitrin among the most abundant detected constituents. The extract reduced IC₅₀ value of in all tested cell lines, with the strongest cytotoxic effect observed in A549 cells. It increased apoptotic cell populations and promoted G0/G1 cell-cycle accumulation, particularly in A549 cells. The extract also markedly suppressed migration and invasion in A549 and MDA-MB-231 cells. These functional effects were accompanied by changes in TP53 and CDKN1A mRNA expression. CONCLUSIONS: E. petrophila ethanol extract shows preliminary antiproliferative, pro-apoptotic, anti-migratory, and anti-invasive activity in selected cancer cell models. However, because the findings are based on crude extract testing and transcript-level analyses, the results should be interpreted as preliminary and correlative. Further work should include extract standardization, LC-MS/MS method validation, broader normal-cell toxicity profiling, active-compound isolation, protein-level mechanistic assays, and in vivo safety and efficacy studies.

papers.abstract_en: Single-cell transfection technologies hold tremendous promise for precision cell and immunotherapies. However, monolithic integration of cell isolation with targeted intracellular delivery remains technically challenging, especially within complex biological matrices. Herein, we present a microcapillary-assisted acoustoelectric single-cell selective isolation and sonoporative transfection platform (μC-ASSIST), which seamlessly sequences microcapillary-assisted dielectrophoresis (μC-DEP) for deterministic single-cell trapping with high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) for transient membrane poration within a unified workflow. We demonstrate the label-free, high-efficiency extraction of human non-small cell lung cancer (A549) cells from a complex white blood cell (WBC) background with a capture efficiency of 95%. Furthermore, we validate the highly efficient, contact-free intracellular delivery of diverse cargoes ranging from small dyes (PI) to functional small interfering RNA (siRNA) and large plasmid DNA (mRFP-C3), maintaining a high cell viability of 83.7% alongside a 78.1% transfection efficiency. Crucially, the targeted delivery of siBcl-xL significantly suppressed target mRNA expression and profoundly inhibited tumor cell motility. By circumventing off-target effects and cumbersome manual handling, the μC-ASSIST platform establishes a highly versatile, streamlined paradigm for precision single-cell engineering, holding immense potential for advancing functional genomics and next-generation gene therapies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Black and Hispanic people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF) experience worse health outcomes. Health disparities are exacerbated by clinical research that does not adequately represent the diversity of the CF population. RESEARCH QUESTIONS: How do Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino(a) PwCF perceive clinical research? What are the barriers and facilitators to participation in research? Are there viable solutions to improve inclusion? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Semi-structured, individual interviews were conducted with PwCF aged ≥18 years who identify as Black/African American race and/or Hispanic/Latino(a) ethnicity. Participants were recruited from six geographically diverse CF centers and through CF Foundation Community Voice, a CF community partner organization. The interview guide was created by a committee that included minoritized PwCF, research coordinators, and physician-scientists. Thematic analysis with inductive and deductive coding was used to analyze interview transcripts. RESULTS: Twenty PwCF were interviewed from 2024 to 2025. Drawing from a race-conscious adaptation of the Behavioral Model for Vulnerable Populations, we used domains of predisposing, need-based, and healthcare environment factors, as well as emergent themes relating to information and support needs. Participants discussed barriers to research participation that included narrow eligibility criteria (e.g., genotype requirements, health status) and logistical challenges such as time and cost. PwCF described a sense of isolation as persons of color with CF, which impacted sense of trust in CF care and research studies. They highlighted that racialized experiences, especially doubt surrounding their CF diagnosis, significantly impact willingness to participate. Solutions center around providing community support to address feelings of isolation and information needs to provide transparency about study design and intent. INTERPRETATION: Participation in clinical research is strongly influenced by an interplay of social, cultural, health, and systemic factors. Solutions to improve inclusion in trials center the needs of marginalized communities across all phases of study design and implementation.

papers.reason: 为溶瘤病毒靶向递送与IL-12免疫治疗提供临床前概念验证，可作为胸部肿瘤免疫治疗新策略的科研参考，但不直接改变当前临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: The lack of tumor-specific targeting by oncolytic viruses (OVs) restricts their therapeutic potential. Here, we report a "cap-linker" strategy to modify the vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) glycoprotein (G protein, VSV-GIN). The modified VSV (Pro-VSVIN) loses its ability to infect cells until present in the tumor microenvironment, where the linker is cleaved by tumor-enriched matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs). When Pro-VSVIN is armed with a single-chain IL-12 (Pro-VSVIN-IL-12) and systemically injected into MC38 tumor-bearing mice, Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 eradicates established tumors while avoiding systemic toxicity, and elicits long-term anti-tumor immune memory. Systemic administration of Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 also markedly inhibits the growth of metastatic cancers in the lung. The efficacy of Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 was further improved when combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade. Compared to WT VSVIN that carries IL-12, intravenously injected Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 leads to strong Th1 immunity, near abolishment of regulatory T cells, and potent CD8+ T cell activation and clonal expansion in tumors. This preclinical work demonstrates a new tumor-specific targeting strategy of VSV for enhanced immunotherapy safety with superior efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: Organoid technology has emerged as a research hotspot in the biomedical field in recent years, providing important methodologies for disease modeling, drug screening, and regenerative medicine. Alveolar organoids serve as crucial models for studying respiratory diseases, and their technological evolution and application expansion reflect key advances in this field. This article systematically reviews the developmental history of organoids, provides an in-depth comparison of the applicability and limitations of different culture and characterization strategies for alveolar organoids, summarizes and critically analyzes alveolar organoid models established for common respiratory diseases, and offers perspectives on future directions in this area.

papers.title_en: The Efferocytosis-Driven Macrophage Polarization: A Concerto in the Tumor Immunosuppressive Microenvironment.
papers.authors: Chen Q, Wu C, Huang C, Zhou H
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Basic Medical Sciences Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine Chengdu China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 本文全面理解胞葬作用调控巨噬细胞极化的机制，增进对肿瘤免疫逃逸基本机制的认识，并为开发靶向胞葬作用的抗癌治疗提供重要指导。
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，无系统检索策略、纳入排除标准、偏倚风险评估或定量合并；对“临床转化现状”及药物与化疗/免疫治疗协同或拮抗原因的评述缺少可核验数据；将机制推论表述为治疗开发指导，证据层级有限。信息不足：无具体药物、试验或疗效数据。
papers.reason: 为理解放化疗后凋亡细胞清除如何驱动M2型巨噬细胞极化、免疫抑制与治疗耐药提供机制框架，可用于提出联合靶向胞葬作用的转化研究假设；不直接改变胸外科临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: Efferocytosis plays a critical role in maintaining tissue homeostasis and controlling inflammation. However, in the tumor microenvironment, this process is hijacked to promote immune suppression. Treatments like radiotherapy and chemotherapy lead to widespread tumor cell death, which triggers efferocytosis and drives macrophages into an immunosuppressive state, allowing the tumor to evade the immune system and resist treatment. Nonetheless, the way efferocytic signals alter macrophage function and promote protumor effects during the recognition, engulfment, and digestion of apoptotic cells remains largely unclear. Therefore, this review thoroughly examines the influence of signaling molecules during the three stages of efferocytosis on macrophage phenotype and function. Subsequently, we explore the impact of polarized M2-type macrophages on shaping the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and regulating the development of drug resistance. Additionally, we critically evaluate the current status of clinical translation of efferocytosis receptor-related drugs and analyze the potential reasons for their synergistic or antagonistic interactions with chemotherapy and immunotherapy. This study provides a comprehensive understanding of the regulatory mechanisms of efferocytosis in macrophage polarization, enhancing knowledge of the fundamental mechanisms underlying tumor immune evasion and offering important guidance for the development of anticancer therapies targeting the efferocytosis process.

papers.title_en: Nephrometry scores differ in their association with warm ischemia time during robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: comparison of RENAL, RPN, PADUA, and SPARE.
papers.authors: Komeya M, Kobayashi K, Jikuya R, Tatenuma T, Noguchi G, Ito H, Ito Y, Muraoka K et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Urology, Yokohama City University Hospital, Yokohama, Japan.
papers.results: RPN与WIT相关性最强（ρ=0.553），其次为肿瘤直径（ρ=0.519）；两者差异很小（Δρ=0.034，95% CI -0.020至0.089）。单预测因子模型中RPN的校正R²最高（0.341）。四种评分均改善基线模型，数值上改善最大者为PADUA（Δ校正R²=0.096；Δ交叉验证RMSE=-0.397 min）。
papers.authors_conclusion: RPN与WIT的独立相关性最强，但其相关性并未明确强于肿瘤直径；每种肾脏测量评分均在肿瘤直径和常规临床变量之外提供额外信息，各系统增量改善幅度不同。
papers.ai_note: 以热缺血时间为唯一结局，属术中操作替代指标，非患者相关临床结局（肾功能、并发症），临床解释力有限；仅纳入四种评分数据齐全者，存在选择偏倚且样本代表性不明；未报告Δ校正R²或ΔRMSE的置信区间/统计检验，无法判断各评分增量差异是否超出随机波动；术者经验、阻断策略、肿瘤内生比例等混杂仅部分调整；单中心回顾性设计限制外推，且未见外部验证。

pico.p: 2016-2023年单中心579例单发肿瘤机器人辅助肾部分切除术（RAPN）病例，且四种评分数据完整
pico.ic: 比较RENAL、RPN、PADUA、SPARE四种肾脏测量评分（并以肿瘤直径及年龄、性别、BMI、侧别、术者经验、手术入路、财年为基线变量/对照），结局为连续性热缺血时间（WIT）

papers.reason: 该研究提示常用肾脏测量评分相对于单纯肿瘤直径的增量信息有限，可约束“评分越复杂越优”的想当然假设，并为同类影像/解剖评分与术中指标关联研究提供方法学参照（配对bootstrap+交叉验证+增量模型）；对胸部肿瘤本身无直接临床影响。
papers.abstract_en: Nephrometry systems are widely used before robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), but their relation to intraoperative complexity may differ. We compared RENAL, RPN, PADUA, and SPARE using continuous warm ischemia time (WIT) and assessed whether the scores added information beyond tumor diameter and routine clinical variables. We retrospectively analyzed 579 single-tumor RAPN cases with complete data for all four scores (2016-2023). Associations with WIT were assessed using Spearman correlations and patient-level paired bootstrap comparisons. Tumor diameter was evaluated as an additional comparator. Incremental value was assessed by adding each nephrometry score to a baseline model containing tumor diameter, age, sex, body mass index, laterality, surgeon experience, surgical approach, and fiscal year. Model performance was evaluated using adjusted R² and 10-fold cross-validation. RPN showed the strongest correlation with WIT (ρ = 0.553), followed by tumor diameter (ρ = 0.519). The difference between them was small (Δρ = 0.034, 95% CI - 0.020 to 0.089). RPN had the highest adjusted R² (0.341) among single-predictor models. All four scores improved the baseline model; the numerically largest improvement was observed with PADUA (Δ adjusted R²=0.096; Δ cross-validated RMSE = - 0.397 min). RPN had the strongest stand-alone association with WIT, but its correlation was not clearly stronger than that of tumor diameter. Each nephrometry score added information beyond tumor diameter and routine clinical variables, with the magnitude of incremental improvement differing among systems.

papers.reason: 为DNAJC9作为泛癌免疫相关标志物及肺癌PI3K/AKT上游调控因子提供初步生信与体外证据，可作为后续肺癌生物标志物或靶点研究的假设来源，但不足以影响临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: Background: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) modulate apoptosis, proliferation, and differentiation, positioning them as potential therapeutic targets in cancer. As a member of the J-domain-containing HSP40 family, DnaJ homolog, subfamily C, member 9 (DNAJC9) has not yet been systematically investigated in a pan-cancer context. Method: Multiple public repositories were employed to perform a comprehensive pan-cancer investigation of DNAJC9. We also utilized single-cell datasets to explore how DNAJC9 expression varies across distinct cellular clusters. These efforts covered several key dimensions, including diagnostic and prognostic value, immune landscape, genomic alterations, methylation differences, and pathway enrichment. To determine its biological effects, DNAJC9 was silenced in lung cancer cell lines, and subsequent experiments assessed cellular phenotypes. The downstream PI3K/AKT signaling cascade was examined via western blotting. Results: Across multiple tumor types, DNAJC9 was markedly upregulated, especially in advanced-stage cases, and higher expression levels predicted worse prognosis. DNAJC9 expression also correlated significantly with immune infiltration, tumor mutation burden (TMB), and microsatellite instability (MSI). Tumor tissues showed substantially lower DNAJC9 methylation than normal tissues. Single-cell analysis detected DNAJC9 expression in multiple immune cell subsets. Knockdown of DNAJC9 in A549 and H1299 lung cancer cells impaired proliferation, migration, and invasion. Functional enrichment analysis then pointed to the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Western blotting further confirmed that silencing DNAJC9 reversed the activated PI3K/AKT cascade in these cells, as shown by decreased p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT ratios. Conclusions: Pan-cancer analyses suggest that DNAJC9 may serve as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker across cancers. Importantly, its role as an upstream PI3K/AKT activator and its functional validation in lung cancer support DNAJC9 as a potential target for anti-cancer drug discovery in this malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: Immunotherapy regimens containing the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor pembrolizumab are widely utilised in the management of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the administration of pembrolizumab is associated with unique immune-related adverse events. Adrenal insufficiency is a rare, potentially life-threatening endocrinopathy that can manifest even after the cessation of planned treatment. A male in his 50s with metastatic pulmonary adenocarcinoma developed an acute adrenal crisis 12 days after completing a 24-month course of pembrolizumab immunotherapy. Routine outpatient blood tests first identified critical hypocortisolaemia (morning serum cortisol <50 nmol/L), prompting the patient to attend hospital. The patient subsequently developed severe hypotension (58/45 mmHg) and reported malaise, anorexia, and vomiting after oral intake. Septic shock was considered but felt to be less likely given the absence of infective symptoms. The patient was successfully resuscitated in the emergency department with administration of fluids and high-dose intravenous hydrocortisone. Following clinical stabilisation, under the supervision of the endocrinology team, he was transitioned to a long-term oral maintenance regimen consisting of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. This case illustrates that pembrolizumab-associated adrenal insufficiency can present as an abrupt, life-threatening crisis in the immediate post-treatment phase. Frontline clinicians must remain vigilant for late-onset endocrinopathies, regardless of the treatment completion date. Proactive patient education and long-term biochemical surveillance are imperative to ensuring early clinical intervention and avoiding catastrophic management delays and poor clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Enteric‑type thymic adenocarcinoma (ETAC) is a rare subtype of thymic carcinoma. It shares highly similar histological and immunophenotypic features with intestinal adenocarcinoma, and is therefore prone to being misdiagnosed as metastatic carcinoma of gastrointestinal origin. Herein, we report a case of advanced ETAC with axillary lymph node oligometastasis. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) and gastrointestinal endoscopy were performed to rule out primary gastrointestinal malignancy. The patient underwent median sternotomy with extended thymectomy, which effectively relieved superior vena cava obstruction and cardiopulmonary compressive symptoms. Postoperatively, systemic chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy, as well as regional radiotherapy targeting the primary tumor bed and metastatic lymph nodes, were administered. The patient remained disease‑free during the 24‑month postoperative follow‑up. This case suggests that aggressive local therapy combined with molecular‑subtype‑based systemic treatment may offer novel therapeutic opportunities for carefully selected patients with advanced ETAC and oligometastases. .

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to examine the experiences of individuals living with cancer across biopsychosocial dimensions and to understand the meanings they attributed to spirituality and their forms of spiritual coping within the illness process. METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted using a phenomenological design. Thirteen patients with cancer were recruited from a public hospital using criterion sampling, a purposive sampling strategy. Data were collected through individual, face-to-face, semi-structured in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological analysis method. The sample size was determined based on data saturation. RESULTS: As a result of data analysis, three themes (perception of cancer and reactions to the process, biopsychosocial effects of the disease, and coping with cancer and spiritual resilience) and nine subthemes (initial perception of cancer, changing perception over time, starting treatment, recurrence experience, physical effects, psychological effects, social effects, spiritual coping methods, and perception of coping) were identified. CONCLUSION: The findings showed that living with cancer is a multidimensional process shaped by changing perceptions and reactions and interconnected physical, psychological, and social difficulties. Spirituality emerged as a personal coping resource used by some participants to give meaning to the illness experience, maintain hope, and find strength to endure. However, differences in participants' perceptions of coping indicated that the use of spiritual resources was not always accompanied by a strong perception of coping. These findings highlight the importance of addressing the changing biopsychosocial needs and personal coping resources of individuals living with cancer through an individualized and holistic approach.

papers.abstract_en: Antibiotics are believed to affect host physiology by altering the gut microbiota. However, it remains unclear which effects of antibiotics are microbiota dependent and which are microbiota independent. Here we present a resource encompassing host and microbiota responses to antibiotic treatment and a computational tool with which to analyse them. Metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses of conventional and germ-free mice revealed that antibiotic administration routes and their combinations affect host and microbiota responses. We developed CompoRes-a computational tool that distinguishes the microbiota-independent impact of antibiotic-induced perturbations, revealing that antibiotics directly impact host physiology. We found that diurnal expression of major histocompatibility complex class II in the mouse colon is controlled by glucose via feeding. This pattern was lost during antibiotic treatment as vancomycin altered feeding behaviour in a microbiota-independent and evolutionarily conserved manner. Together, our study establishes a direct, non-microbial pathway by which antibiotics reshape host immunity and circadian physiology.

papers.abstract_en: TRIM22 is a TRIM family E3 ubiquitin ligase whose expression is strongly induced by interferons. For many years, it has been identified primarily as an antiviral effector, a role that remains well validated. A growing body of cancer-related work now forces us to expand that view considerably. Depending on tumor type, upstream signaling context, and the specific substrates available in a given cell, TRIM22 can either constrain malignancy or actively promote it. In breast, colorectal, ovarian, endometrial, hepatocellular, cervical, and gastric cancers, as well as in certain lung tumor subsets, TRIM22 is frequently downregulated or functionally impaired. Where this occurs, its re-expression tends to curb proliferation, invasion, stemness, and cachexia-associated programs. Conversely, in non-small-cell lung carcinoma, glioblastoma, melanoma, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, TRIM22 often takes on a pro-tumorigenic role. It drives epithelial mesenchymal transition, NF-κB signaling, autophagy, and acquired resistance to chemotherapy or targeted agents. The substrate repertoire of TRIM22 is remarkably broad. It includes p53-related effectors, I-κBα, NF-κB components, β-catenin, TCF4, CCS-STAT3, PHLPP2, Raf-1, p21, ADRB2, CDT2, and Smad2. In this review, we synthesize recent findings and argue that TRIM22 functions as a stress-responsive ubiquitin signaling hub rather than as a conventional oncogene or tumor suppressor. It integrates inputs from interferons, p53, hormonal cues, and inflammatory pathways. The phenotypic outcome, whether tumor suppression or tumor promotion, is dictated by cellular lineage and the pre-existing molecular wiring. Deciphering this contextual logic is the key to translating TRIM22 biology into clinically useful strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Atomically precise metal clusters hold great promise for cancer theranostics, yet current strategies for introducing tumor-targeting functionality often compromise their structural precision. Herein, an erlotinib (Er)-functionalized gold cluster, Au8-Er, is constructed through ligand engineering for targeted non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) theranostics. The Er ligands endow Au8-Er with high affinity toward the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), enabling selective tumor targeting and preferential accumulation at lung tumor sites. Under the glutathione-rich tumor microenvironment, Au8-Er releases Er to achieve chemotherapy. Simultaneously, the cluster exhibits strong X-ray attenuation and oxygen-sensitive phosphorescence, allowing it to function as both an X-ray scintillator and a photosensitizer for efficient X-ray-induced photodynamic therapy (X-PDT) under low-dose irradiation. Moreover, its X-ray-excited luminescence enables high-contrast imaging. The synergistic integration of targeted chemotherapy, X-PDT, and imaging within a structurally precise nanoplatform results in enhanced therapeutic efficacy against NSCLC. This work highlights ligand engineering as an effective strategy for imparting biological functionality to atomically precise metal clusters and advances their application in precision cancer theranostics.

papers.abstract_en: In-stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major complication following vascular interventions, with neointimal hyperplasia representing a central pathological process that can adversely affect postoperative outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that neointimal hyperplasia is driven by vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic transition, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and multiple forms of programmed cell death. Despite substantial advances, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This review comprehensively examines neointimal hyperplasia from the perspectives of epidemiology, pathophysiology, preclinical animal models, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies. Particular attention is given to the emerging associations between recently characterized forms of programmed cell death, including ferroptosis and cuproptosis, and neointimal hyperplasia. In addition, commonly used preclinical animal models are reviewed, together with potential therapeutic approaches such as colchicine and vasostatin-2 and their underlying mechanisms. The diagnostic roles of invasive imaging and noninvasive modalities in evaluating neointimal hyperplasia are discussed, with emphasis on their respective advantages and limitations. Furthermore, current stent-based strategies, pharmacological therapies, and alternative interventions for ISR are summarized, along with critical consideration of their limitations and potential avenues for improvement. By integrating mechanistic evidence with available therapeutic options, this review aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for the clinical management of ISR.

papers.abstract_en: Neonatal respiratory diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in intensive care settings, with management complicated by the limitations of current monitoring tools. Chest radiography provides only static snapshots and cannot capture the dynamic evolution of lung aeration, while lung ultrasound, though portable, remains operator-dependent and incapable of quantifying regional ventilation. Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) has emerged as a noninvasive, radiation free imaging modality that addresses these gaps by enabling real time, continuous visualization of regional lung function at the bedside. This review synthesises evidence from studies published between 2011 and 2026, examining how EIT informs the management of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome, acute respiratory distress syndrome, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, pneumothorax, and the transitions inherent to mechanical ventilation. Across these disease contexts, EIT reveals regional ventilation heterogeneity invisible to conventional monitors, provides immediate physiological feedback during therapeutic interventions, and enables early detection of complications before clinical deterioration. We identify key barriers to clinical adoption, including technical limitations, lack of standardised protocols, and the need for outcome driven trials, and propose a research agenda to accelerate translation. By reframing EIT not merely as an imaging tool but as a dynamic decision support system integrated into clinical workflows, we aim to provide clinicians with a framework for leveraging this technology to improve outcomes in the most vulnerable patients.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Deep learning models can predict the functional impact of genetic variants. However, training and applying these sequence models to personalized genome sequences are severely constrained by the computational burden of storing and reading massive datasets. RESULTS: We developed GenVarLoader, an accelerated dataloader that creates personalized genomic sequences and functional tracks on-the-fly to overcome these bottlenecks. GenVarLoader stores this personalized genomic data in formats specifically optimized for machine learning. Our tool reads variants up to 26,000 times faster than a pre-subset BCF, loads personalized data up to 130 times faster than tuned FASTA and pyBigWig pipelines, and reduces storage approximately 2,000-fold compared to existing alternatives. CONCLUSIONS: By eliminating severe data loading bottlenecks, GenVarLoader ensures efficient model training and inference. It provides a scalable solution for integrating biobank-scale personalized genomic data with deep learning applications.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a common complication of pregnancy; however, its exact molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Excessive lactate accumulation in the placenta is often observed during FGR. High concentrations of lactate can regulate the proliferation of pathological cells through lactylation of key proteins. Therefore, we aimed to screen key lactylation modification-related genes (LMRGs) and provide new directions for the diagnosis and treatment of FGR. METHODS: The Differentially expressed LMRGs (DE-LMRGs) in FGR were evaluated using the Gene Expression Omnibus database. Functional enrichment analysis was performed, and a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was created to explore the characteristics of placental gene networks associated with FGR. In addition, secondary cluster analysis was performed using a machine learning algorithm to screen critical genes. We evaluated the degree of immune cell infiltration of key genes using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. The expression and function of key genes in FGR were verified experimentally. Furthermore, FUBP1 lactylation was assessed using mass spectrometry and immunoprecipitation. We overexpressed wild-type and mutant FUBP1 in HTR-8/SVneo cells to investigate how its lactylation regulates trophoblast function. Finally, patient-derived organoids (PDO) were cultured to confirm the underlying mechanism of FUBP1. RESULTS: In total, 35 DE-LMRGs were identified, and their PPI network was constructed. Two distinct FGR clusters were obtained using unsupervised consensus clustering. Moreover, the DE-LMRGs between the two patterns were mainly enriched in immune cell regulation-related molecular functions. We identified 5 overlapping key genes (BCLAF1, FUBP1, S100A6, CSRP1, CSRP2) by integrating the LASSO, random forest (RF), and SVM-RFE algorithms and screening for genes with a large fold change (using log2-FC). FUBP1 and BCLAF1 expression was lower in FGR placental tissues than in normal controls. Functional assays showed that both genes typically promote HTR-8/SVneo cell proliferation and invasion. However, lactylation of FUBP1 exerted the opposite effect by inhibiting proliferation and invasion and promoting apoptosis, indicating that FUBP1 lactylation regulates trophoblast function. Furthermore, PDO derived from the trophoblast tissues of patients with FGR revealed that FUBP1 lactylation suppressed PDO formation. CONCLUSIONS: FUBP1 lactylation is identified as a novel mechanism suppressing trophoblast function in FGR. This finding expands the field of FGR research by highlighting the role of lactylation-modified proteins and provides crucial insights into the pathological mechanisms of FGR.

papers.abstract_en: Eukaryotic cells contain various membrane- and non-membrane-bound organelles, whose spatial and functional organization underpins intracellular homeostasis. Organelle coordination is governed by complex signaling and metabolic networks, often facilitated by direct physical contacts and molecular exchange. Mitochondria, as central hubs of bioenergetic and metabolic activity, are essential to functional coordination among cellular organelles. They engage in diverse cellular processes, encompassing ATP production, biosynthesis of key metabolites, calcium ion buffering, redox balance, and cellular turnover. To preserve their integrity and functionality, dysfunctional mitochondria undergo selective elimination via mitophagy, a specialized form of macroautophagy. Mitophagy plays dual roles in maintaining mitochondrial fidelity and actively shapes interorganelle communication. Through bidirectional signaling, mitophagy influences the activity of multiple organelles, including the endoplasmic reticulum, nucleus, lysosomes, peroxisomes, and lipid droplets. This interorganelle crosstalk is essential for adapting to metabolic stress, maintaining redox balance, and coordinating cell fate decisions. In this review, we explore the intricate signaling networks connecting mitophagy with various organelles and discuss how these interactions influence organ function and overall cellular health. We also highlight emerging small-molecule modulators of mitophagy, providing insight into potential therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing organelle communication in pathological conditions.

papers.abstract_en: Fetal brain MRI commonly uses thick-slice acquisitions to mitigate motion artifacts and preserve in-plane image quality. Multiple motion-corrupted stacks of 2D slices can be retrospectively reconstructed into isotropic 3D volumes; however, volumes reconstructed from thicker slices generally exhibit lower image quality than those reconstructed from thinner slices because limited through-plane information results in residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. Existing post-reconstruction denoising methods are limited by their dependence on large-scale datasets comprising noisy-clean image pairs or insufficient modeling of inter-slice structural consistency. In this work, we propose a Pseudo-Warping Field Guided Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Network (PW-GAN), which formulates post-reconstruction denoising as unpaired translation between low- and high-quality MRI domains. By incorporating a pseudo-warping field module, our method significantly enhances inter-slice continuity in the reconstructed volumes while effectively suppressing residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. On simulated data, PW-GAN achieved a PSNR of 39.65 dB and an SSIM of 0.9932. On real clinical data, it reduced the inter-slice warping error by up to 40% compared with unsupervised baselines. These results demonstrate that PW-GAN outperforms existing unsupervised models and achieves performance comparable to several state-of-the-art supervised methods. Qualitatively, PW-GAN produced cleaner results with smoother inter-slice structural transitions while preserving anatomical structures, demonstrating its effectiveness in post-reconstruction denoising of fetal brain MRI acquired from thick-slice scans.

papers.abstract_en: Current light-based devices, such as laser hair removal, intense pulsed light (IPL), vascular laser therapy, and dermatologic phototherapy, are widely used in clinical dermatology but rely heavily on subjective manual parameterization or uncalibrated point-based colorimeters. To overcome these limitations, this work presents a unified system for hair segmentation and skin characterization in macroscopic dermatological images. Unlike most existing literature that relies on dermoscopic datasets captured under highly controlled conditions, our approach is specifically designed for macroscopic images that replicate real clinical laser treatments. The proposed pipeline integrates a custom-trained variant of the YOLOv9 deep learning architecture for instance segmentation and classical image processing within a single workflow to extract objective skin and hair parameters such as phototype, hair density, color, and thickness. A color calibration stage using spectrophotometric measurements ensures accurate feature estimation regardless of illumination conditions. Experimental results show competitive segmentation metrics (mAP@50 ≈ 0.80) on a custom dataset featuring short, shaved hairs, typical of pre-treatment scenarios. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed pipeline in providing the objective, foundational skin and hair features required for future automated laser parameterization, paving the way for its extension to broader light-based medical therapies.

papers.authors: Venkatesharao SM, Jayaraman A
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pharmacology, M.

papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disorder strongly mediated by genetic susceptibility and aberrant epithelial repair mechanisms. Among the identified genetic factors, the MUC5B promoter polymorphism rs35705950 represents the most significant and frequently replicated risk variant associated with both familial and sporadic IPF. This review focuses on the mechanistic role of MUC5B dysregulation in promoting epithelial dysfunction and profibrotic signalling, with particular emphasis on its interaction with transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signalling and KL-6-associated epithelial injury. Excessive MUC5B expression within distal airways disrupts mucociliary homeostasis, prolongs epithelial exposure to inhaled toxic stimuli, and enhances persistent alveolar stress, thereby facilitating chronic epithelial injury and aberrant tissue repair. Sustained epithelial damage subsequently activates TGF-β-mediated SMAD signalling pathways, promoting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and extracellular matrix deposition. Emerging evidence further suggests a close relationship between MUC5B-associated epithelial dysfunction and elevated KL-6 expression, indicating that KL-6 may function as a downstream biomarker indicating ongoing epithelial injury and fibrotic progression. The proposed MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 mechanistic signaling provides an integrated molecular network linking genetic susceptibility, epithelial dysfunction, biomarker elevation, and progressive fibrosis in IPF. In addition, telomere-related and surfactant-associated gene mutations further lead to epithelial instability and impaired regenerative capacity. Together, these interconnected molecular mechanisms provide significant insights into IPF progression and may support the development of biomarker-driven prognostic approaches and targeted precision therapies for improved disease management.

papers.affiliation_highlight: College of Medicine, QU Health, Qatar University, Doha, 2713, Qatar.
papers.authors_conclusion: These emerging preclinical findings implicate EGFR as a promising therapeutic target to complement or extend beyond VEGF-centered approaches. Further validation of the role of EGFR and its ligands in mediating retinal pathology in clinically relevant models will be essential for advancing EGFR-targeted interventions toward clinical translation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a major cause of preventable vision loss worldwide and arises from the convergence of chronic inflammation, oxidative injury, and metabolic dysregulation that ultimately compromises vascular and neuronal integrity of the retina. Although intravitreal anti-VEGF agents have improved the management of DR, significant limitations such as incomplete therapeutic response, repeated administration and high cost underscore the need for alternative or adjunctive strategies. MAIN BODY: Emerging preclinical evidence suggests that dysregulated signaling via the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) plays a critical role in DR pathogenesis. EGFR and some of its ligands are expressed across multiple retinal cell types and play important roles in normal development and in regulating homeostasis in adult retinas. However, in hyperglycemia/diabetes enhanced EGFR signaling promotes vascular hyperpermeability, pericyte loss, glial reactivity, inflammatory amplification, and pro-fibrotic remodeling that contributes to both early microvascular dysfunction and later proliferative changes in experimental models. Several preclinical studies indicate that pharmacologic blockade of EGFR or downstream signaling pathways attenuates angiogenesis, inflammation, and gliosis in models of DR. CONCLUSIONS: These emerging preclinical findings implicate EGFR as a promising therapeutic target to complement or extend beyond VEGF-centered approaches. Further validation of the role of EGFR and its ligands in mediating retinal pathology in clinically relevant models will be essential for advancing EGFR-targeted interventions toward clinical translation.
