papers.abstract_en: Respirable crystalline silica (RCS) is a major occupational health hazard associated with silicosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), lung cancer, autoimmune diseases, and other systemic disorders. Saudi Arabia is undergoing rapid industrial expansion in sectors with substantial potential for RCS exposure, including mining, construction, cement production, glass manufacturing, oil and gas, engineered stone fabrication, and photovoltaic manufacturing. This review evaluates the potential risk of occupational RCS exposure in Saudi Arabia by integrating evidence from the scientific literature, government reports, labor and mining statistics, mineralogical data, and regulatory documents. The novel silica Hazard triangle framework was applied to assess three principal determinants of occupational exposure: workforce distribution, silica-containing materials, and high-risk industrial activities. Saudi Arabia possesses extensive reserves of high-purity silica sand, and continued expansion of mining and downstream silica-based industries may increase occupational exposure potential. The kingdom's arid climate may also contribute to dust generation and increase the occupational exposure of RCS. Although documented cases of silicosis confirm that silica-related disease exists in Saudi Arabia, published evidence on occupational exposure assessment, epidemiology, and health surveillance remains limited. International regulatory developments demonstrate the importance of health-based occupational exposure limits (OELs), exposure monitoring, engineering controls, and medical surveillance. Current Saudi labor law, National Council for occupational safety and health (NCOSH) policies, and General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) occupational disease frameworks provide an important legal and institutional foundation for the future development of silica-specific occupational health regulations. This review identifies important knowledge gaps and highlights the need for comprehensive exposure assessment, strengthened industrial hygiene capacity, and evidence-based regulatory strategies to reduce the future burden of silica-related diseases while supporting sustainable industrial development in Saudi Arabia.

papers.abstract_en: Proton boron capture therapy (PBCT), based on proton-boron fusion reactions (11B + p →3α + 8.7 MeV), has the potential to enhance the biological effectiveness of proton therapy. To achieve this potential, the efficient delivery of enough 11B to cancer cells will be paramount. This study demonstrates a newly developed method of poor solvent-mediated spontaneous assembly of polymeric micelles with entrapped o-carborane, in which ethanol is a good solvent for the payload o-carborane but a poor solvent for the hydrophobic segment poly(ε-caprolactone) in this amphiphilic block copolymer. This method provided smaller polymeric micelles compared to use of tetrahydrofuran, a good solvent for the amphiphilic block copolymer, as the sole solvent for both payload and copolymer. The prepared nanoscale formulation enabled the boron-rich cage compound o-carborane to be effectively delivered to tumor cells, and its enhancement of the biological effectiveness of proton therapy was preliminarily validated in a pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell line, MiaPaCa-2, by survival assays and DNA damage assessment. The 111In-labeled congener was also successfully prepared and used in biodistribution assays in normal mice, opening the way to further studies on image-guided PBCT in preclinical animal models.

papers.authors: Peng S, Wang L, Ouyang J, Liu R
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Neurosurgery Peking University People's Hospital, Xicheng District Beijing China.
papers.authors_conclusion: Defining functionally validated astrocyte states and developing biomarker-guided, stage-adaptive therapies may enable more precise intervention in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Astrocytes have emerged as central regulators of neuroinflammation, extending far beyond their traditional roles as structural and metabolic support cells. In neurological disorders, astrocytes undergo reactive remodeling that encompasses morphological, transcriptional, metabolic, and functional changes. Rather than fitting into a fixed A1/A2 dichotomy, reactive astrocytes exist along a disease-, region-, and stage-dependent continuum shaped by local pathology and intercellular crosstalk. This review summarizes how astrocytes contribute to neuroinflammatory processes in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, central nervous system injury, infection, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder. We highlight convergent mechanisms, including cytokine and chemokine release, complement activation, glutamate and ion homeostasis disruption, oxidative stress, metabolic reprogramming, and blood-brain barrier regulation, while emphasizing disease-specific astrocytic programs. We further discuss astrocyte interactions with microglia, neurons, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells, and peripheral immune cells, as well as key regulatory pathways, epigenetic remodeling, and lipid-dependent metabolic signaling. Finally, we evaluate current and emerging astrocyte-targeted therapeutic strategies, including metabolic modulation, receptor targeting, gene editing, nanodelivery, and gut-brain axis interventions. Defining functionally validated astrocyte states and developing biomarker-guided, stage-adaptive therapies may enable more precise intervention in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Large insert gene editing in ex vivo, primary human T cells represents an important approach for engineering next-generation cellular immunotherapies. While CRISPR-based editing is well-established for small genetic modifications, large insert knock-in remains a technical bottleneck. This review examines current strategies for achieving efficient, precise and safe integration of large genetic elements. We compare delivery methods for CRISPR components, highlighting electroporation of Cas9 ribonucleoproteins as the most efficient but often cytotoxic approach; emerging alternatives such as cell-penetrating peptides and lipid nanoparticles offer improved cell viability at the expense of editing efficiency. The influence of genomic locus selection, guide RNA design and chromatin context on editing outcomes, as well as the role of homology-directed repair (HDR) template design is evaluated. Various template formats-including linear double- and single-stranded DNA, plasmids, circular single-stranded (css) DNA and recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV)-are assessed for their efficiency, toxicity and risk of off-target integration. Where possible, cross-study normalisation is used to enable meaningful comparisons. rAAV templates consistently achieve the highest insertion rates but come with concerns regarding cost, size limitations and insertional mutagenesis, whereas non-viral approaches such as cssDNA templates show promise. Additionally, we review the use of small-molecule modulators to enhance HDR efficiency, noting trade-offs between improved insertion rates and potential genomic instability. Overall, successful large insert editing requires balancing of editing efficiency, cell viability and genomic safety considerations. Continued optimisation of delivery systems, template design and repair pathway modulation will be critical for advancing scalable and clinically viable T-cell therapies.

papers.abstract_en: Lactate, once regarded merely as the terminal product of glycolysis, is now recognised as a pivotal immunometabolic regulator that actively shapes inflammatory responses. However, accumulating evidence reveals an apparent paradox that lactate can either amplify immune activation or promote inflammation resolution depending on the biological context. The mechanisms underlying this functional duality remain incompletely understood, limiting the development of effective lactate-targeted therapies. In this review, we propose that lactate functions as a context-dependent immunometabolic rheostat whose Yin-Yang properties are determined by the integration of four key factors: lactate concentration, cellular identity, disease stage and inflammatory microenvironment. We summarise how lactate regulates immune responses through coordinated control of metabolic reprogramming, intercellular lactate shuttling, receptor-mediated signalling, intracellular sensing, and protein lactylation, thereby orchestrating the activation and resolution of inflammation. We further discuss the cell-specific actions of lactate across endothelial cells, macrophages, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, neutrophils, and lymphocytes, highlighting how these mechanisms collectively remodel the inflammatory microenvironment. Beyond mechanistic insights, we examine evidence from representative inflammatory disease models, including rheumatoid arthritis, sepsis, and atherosclerosis, and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lactate production, transport, sensing and metabolism. Rather than advocating indiscriminate lactate inhibition, current evidence supports context-specific modulation of lactate signalling according to disease stage and immune landscape.

papers.abstract_en: T-complex protein 1 (TCP1) encodes the TCP1α subunit, one of eight subunits of the chaperonin containing TCP1 ring complex (TRiC). Heterozygous TCP1 variants cause autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay or intellectual disability, seizures, pyramidal or cerebellar signs, and brain malformations, particularly polymicrogyria. However, the reported clinical spectrum remains limited. We report a 4-year-old girl with global developmental delay, speech and motor delay, behavioral dysregulation, microcephaly, hypotonia with core weakness, and a previously unreported heterozygous likely pathogenic TCP1 variant, c.1392delT (p.A465Qfs*3). This frameshift variant is located in exon 11, truncates the final 16.5% of the protein, is predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay, and is absent from gnomAD. Biological parental testing was unavailable, precluding determination of variant inheritance. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated an absent septum pellucidum with mild bilateral frontal sulcation/gyration asymmetry without polymicrogyria; the optic nerves and pituitary were normal. No seizures were documented through age 4 years. Additional findings included bicuspid aortic valve with mild aortic insufficiency, asthma, severe eczema/atopy, and multiple food allergies. This case suggests that the molecular and neuroimaging spectrum of TCP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder may be broader than previously recognized; however, a causal association between TCP1 and absent septum pellucidum cannot be established from a single case. The relationship of the cardiac and atopic findings to TCP1 remains uncertain. Additional cases and functional studies are needed to clarify genotype-phenotype relationships.

papers.abstract_en: The World Health Organization and the National Advisory Committee on Immunization now recommend a single-dose HPV vaccine schedule for most immunocompetent adolescents. As Canadian jurisdictions transition to a single-dose schedule, we apply a social and behavioral science lens and draw on lessons from previous vaccine schedule changes and international experience to identify potential challenges and opportunities associated with this transition. Key implementation considerations include maintaining public confidence through transparent communication about the rationale for the schedule change, ensuring healthcare providers, immunizers, and parents are adequately prepared to support the transition, and promoting equitable access through robust catch-up programs and targeted outreach initiatives. Attention to these factors will be critical to supporting successful implementation of single-dose HPV vaccination programs in Canada.
